agents.name: Ad Anomaly Watch
agents.description: Owns spend and CPA spikes on live campaigns. Pause or rec. Does not launch a new campaign.
agents.details:
# Ad Anomaly Watch

> Catch the spend and CPA spike on a live campaign before the client sees it on the invoice.

## What it does

Ad Anomaly Watch is a spend-and-CPA anomaly owner for founder-led marketing, creative, and web shops. On the cadence you set it pulls spend, clicks, conversions, and CPA or ROAS for every live campaign in Google Ads and Meta Ads, then flags pacing that will blow the cap, CPA above your threshold, conversion tracking sitting at zero while spend runs, and broken landing pages when a URL check is configured.

It never stops at an alert. Every anomaly comes with exactly one recommendation: pause this ad set or campaign, cut budget to a named number, or wait and watch with a reason. The default is to Slack you the rec and wait. Live spend only gets paused when you have configured that exact kill switch, and this agent never launches a campaign, ad, or keyword.

## What you'll need

- **Meta Ads** — required for Meta campaign pulls, through the Meta Ads MCP.
- **Google Ads** — required for Google campaign pulls. Connected during onboarding; no registry connector, so the agent uses the account access you grant.
- **Slack** — required. Every rec, tracking break, and kill-switch fire lands in your founder channel.
- **Client tracker** — optional. A sheet or tracker that maps accounts to clients and caps.
- **API keys:** none.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut.
2. The `agent-onboarding` skill runs before first use. It asks for your ad accounts, CPA and cap targets per client, what counts as a spike, whether a kill switch exists, and which Slack channel gets the recs, then saves the answers into `AGENTS.md` and `.claude/skills/agent-onboarding/config.json`.
3. Ask for the first run: Check live campaigns for spend and CPA spikes and draft pause-or-rec notes without pausing anything.

Re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

- Check every live campaign for spend and CPA spikes right now
- Which ad sets should we pause or cut today, and why
- Every two hours during business hours, watch live spend and Slack me any spike

## What's inside

- `AGENTS.md` — the agent's operating instructions, safe operating rules, and the `## Your context` block that onboarding fills in.
- `.claude/skills/agent-onboarding/` — the first-run interview that captures your systems, cadence, voice, and approval rules and writes `config.json`.

## Notes

- Built for 2-200 person founder-led agencies that need live spend watched, not another campaign brief.
- The agent never launches a campaign, rewrites the media plan, or hides a tracking break while spend continues.
- No pause or budget change happens without founder approval unless a kill switch you configured has fired.

agents.name: Agent ROI
agents.description: Shows what each of your workspace's agents delivers, what it costs and its return, with a receipt behind every number.
agents.details:
# Agent ROI

An agent that reviews what your workspace's agents deliver and what they cost, with a receipt behind every number.

## What it does

It reads each agent's sessions, counts the finished work (outcomes) each one delivered, and prices it with prices you confirm.
It reads spend from the Gamut Platform usage page.
The dashboard shows cost, worth and return for the same ranges as the usage page: week to date, month to date, and the last 7, 14 and 30 days.

- **Cost** is AI usage and paid tools. People's time is an estimate you can turn on in the Cost panel. It is off by default.
- **Worth** is each outcome times its price, from the low end to the stated price.
- **Return** is worth divided by cost.
- Agents sit in three bands: **Fully counted** (every session in the range read, cost known), **Incomplete** and **Idle**. The totals cover fully counted agents only.
- Every figure opens to its breakdown. Every outcome links to its receipt.

## Setup

Say "Set up Agent ROI". Setup takes three answers:

1. **Scope.** Which agents to review. Reply yes to the proposed groups, or move agents between them.
2. **One form.** What an hour of a person's time is worth, whether your go is enough to read agents' sessions, and whether to sign in to Gamut Platform (owner or admin) for cost or skip it for now.
3. **One table.** The outcome and price drafted for each agent. Reply yes, or say what to fix.

The dashboard opens right after, from a sample of each agent's sessions.
A full read of the last 30 days then runs in the background, about 1 to 2 hours for 15 agents.
Agents move from Incomplete to Fully counted as it finishes.

## Refresh

Nothing runs on a schedule.
Say "refresh the dashboard" in a chat with the agent.
It reads new sessions, re-reads the usage page (you may need to sign in), and tells you what changed.
The dashboard shows when it was last updated, and marks it stale after 24 hours.

## Downloads

The Download menu on the dashboard gives the current range as:
- a one-page PDF to forward
- an agents CSV, one row per agent
- an outcomes CSV, every outcome with its receipt

## What's new in 1.0

- Views follow the Gamut Platform usage page's ranges, defaulting to the last 30 days. Monthly close, statements and monthly reports are gone.
- Refresh is by hand. There is no scheduled run.
- Cost is spend only. People's time is an optional estimate.
- No findings and no cut, keep or invest calls. Each agent shows its return instead.
- Agents are banded Fully counted, Incomplete and Idle.
- Explanations live in tooltips and the About panel.
- Real agent avatars and member stacks, captured from the Gamut app.
- PDF, agents CSV and outcomes CSV downloads.

agents.name: Bill Splitter
agents.description: Finds each shared bill from named senders at month end, works out everyone's share, and hands you one-tap Venmo request links. It never moves money.
agents.details:
# Bill Splitter

> Stop fronting the electric bill and forgetting to collect: every shared bill turns into tap-to-send requests at month end.

## What it does

At the end of each month, Bill Splitter looks for bill emails from the senders you named, such as the utility, the internet provider or a shared subscription. It never searches the rest of your inbox. It reads the amount and due date from the email or the attached statement, and if the amount isn't clear it asks you instead of guessing. Then it works out each person's share with the split you set up: equal, percentages, fixed amounts or custom.

You get one summary with each bill attached or linked, every person's share, and a prefilled Venmo request link for each person, with a short note like "Electric-Aug-2026". The shares always add up to the cent. It flags a bill that jumped from its usual amount and a bill that hasn't arrived yet. You tap each link, check the request in the Venmo app and send it yourself. The agent never messages the people you split with and never moves money.

Prefer Splitwise? It can record each bill there instead, after you approve it.

## What you'll need

- **Gmail or Outlook**: required. Read access limited to the bill senders you name.
- **Venmo**: no connection needed. The agent builds request links that open in your Venmo app.
- **Splitwise**: optional alternative to Venmo links, as a connected account.
- **A place for the summary**: the agent's own email inbox (recommended, so links are tappable on your phone), Slack, Telegram, iMessage or in-app.
- **API keys:** none.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut.
2. The `agent-onboarding` skill runs before first use. It records your bills, who's in each split and their Venmo handles, connects your mailbox, and checks that the request links open correctly on your phone.
3. Ask it to split last month's shared bills so you can check the amounts before the first scheduled run.

Re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

- Split last month's electric and internet bills between the three of us
- Show me this month's shares with Venmo request links for each person
- Change the internet split so Sam pays a flat 20 dollars from next month

## What's inside

- `AGENTS.md`: the month-end routine, splitting rules, Gamut mechanics, safe operating rules and the `## Your context` block.
- `.claude/skills/agent-onboarding/`: first-run setup, the Venmo link check, a supervised split, the schedule and `config.json`.
- `.claude/skills/venmo-request-links/`: the Venmo request link format, encoding, a small builder, first-run verification and fallbacks.

## Notes

- Venmo request links are not officially documented and have changed before. The agent checks them on first run and falls back to copy-ready text if they stop working.
- Links only fill in a request. Nothing is sent until you tap Request in Venmo.
- Late fees and past-due balances are not split unless you say so.

## Privacy

The agent reads only mail from the bill senders you list. Request notes never include account numbers or service addresses. It stores no passwords. If a provider's portal must be opened to read an amount, you sign in yourself, each time.

agents.name: Billing Chaser
agents.description: Owns agency money in: reconstructs unbilled time, chases overdue invoices, flags retainers running low, and drafts the renewal in the same job.
agents.details:
# Billing Chaser

> Get unbilled hours out the door, overdue invoices chased, and the retainer renewal drafted before it quietly expires.

## What it does

Billing Chaser owns agency money in for founder-led marketing, creative and web shops. Every Friday it rebuilds your week's billable time by client from your calendar, sent email and the documents you edited, shows the meeting, thread or file behind each block, labels every number as an estimate, and flags work that looks billable but is not logged in Harvest, Toggl or your time sheet. The recap is read-only; it never creates time entries or invoices on its own.

Once hours are confirmed it drafts the invoice in QuickBooks or Xero. Twice a week it buckets open invoices as current, 1-30, 31-60 and 60+ days past due, keeps a living aging log, and drafts one chase per client per cycle, firmer as it ages, naming the invoice number, amount and due date. Paid accounts and payment plans are skipped, and an invoice counts as paid only once the money has cleared.

It watches hours or dollars left on every retainer and warns at the remaining percent you set (default 20%). When a retainer end date or the client's notice deadline lands inside the renewal window, it drafts the renewal inside this same job. Invoices, chases and renewals all stay in draft until you approve the exact text.

Unlike Invoice Hunter (trades jobs), Invoice Ask (simple chasing) and Ledger Hawk (professional firms), it is built around agency time and retainers.

## What you'll need

- **QuickBooks or Xero** — one is required for open invoices, aging and invoice drafts.
- **Google Calendar and Google Drive** — required for the billable hours recap. Outlook and OneDrive work too.
- **Gmail or Outlook** — required. Sent mail feeds the recap and drafts land in your mailbox.
- **Slack** — the agent posts warnings and escalations from its own Slack app, set up during onboarding. Your own Slack account is only needed if it should read a billing channel.
- **Harvest, Toggl or a time sheet** — recommended, to compare against logged time. Harvest and Toggl connect with an API key.
- **Stripe or HubSpot** — optional, for card payments or retainer records.
- **API keys:** only for Harvest or Toggl, if you use them.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut.
2. The `agent-onboarding` skill runs before first use. It connects your books, time source, calendar, docs and mailbox, builds a client map with you, asks for your rounding, low-retainer percent, renewal window, chase cycle and voice, runs a supervised hours recap and chase, and schedules every routine.
3. Ask for the first run: pull unbilled time, overdue invoices and retainers running low, and draft any renewals due, without sending.

Re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

- Rebuild this week's billable hours by client and show me what's unlogged
- Which retainers are under 20% left, and draft the renewals for any ending soon
- Draft the next chase for every overdue invoice and list the worst offenders

## What's inside

- `AGENTS.md` — the routines (hours recap, unbilled time to invoice, collections, retainer running low, renewal, replies and recap), the Gamut mechanics, safe operating rules, and the `## Your context` block that onboarding fills in.
- `.claude/skills/agent-onboarding/` — the first-run setup: connections, client map, questions, supervised dry run, schedules and triggers, and `config.json`.
- `.claude/skills/time-reconstruction/` — how to rebuild billable time from calendar, email and docs with evidence per block and estimate labels.
- `.claude/skills/collections-playbook/` — aging buckets, the aging log format, the tone ladder, the cleared-payment test, skip rules and the one-chase-per-cycle ledger.

## Notes

- Built for 2-200 person founder-led agencies with time sitting unbilled and retainers that expire quietly.
- Recap hours are estimates for your review and are never invoiced as-is. The agent never writes off hours, discounts a retainer, or sends legal collections language.

agents.name: Calendar Guardian
agents.description: Watches one executive calendar for conflicts, slips and landmines, drafts reschedule emails, and keeps open-time blocks honest without moving real meetings.
agents.details:
# Calendar Guardian

> Know the moment a meeting breaks, get the reschedule email already drafted, and never find an invite you didn't make.

## What it does

Calendar Guardian watches one calendar: yours, or a principal's you manage as an executive assistant. Four routines:

- **Conflict alarm.** On every calendar change it checks for double-bookings on protected commitments, key meetings moved or declined by the other side, in-person meetings with no travel time, missing locations or dial-ins, and anything booked outside hours, on a no-meeting day or over PTO. Real problems arrive ranked and deduplicated. For a true clash it drafts a reschedule email in your mailbox that offers three open slots.
- **Health audit.** Twice each weekday it sweeps the next few business days for unanswered invites, overlaps, missing conferencing, back-to-backs without transit and overloaded days, and sends one briefing. It can color-code the calendar to a scheme you choose. That is off by default.
- **Open-time blocks (optional).** It keeps placeholder "Open" blocks in step with real free time: weekdays, business hours, holidays skipped, gaps of 30 minutes or more. It writes only to blocks it created.
- **Client slip alert (optional).** When a client declines or reschedules by email to a shared inbox, it checks the calendar, then posts once to that client's Slack channel from its own Slack app. If it isn't sure which client it is, it DMs you instead.

It never creates, moves, accepts, declines or deletes a real meeting, and it never sends an email.

## What you'll need

- **Google Calendar or Outlook**: required. Your own calendar, or your access as a delegate to a principal's calendar.
- **Gmail or Outlook mail**: required for the reschedule drafts. A shared inbox account is needed only for the slip alert.
- **Slack**: optional. The agent's own Slack app posts slip alerts and can DM you alerts. Slack read access for audit context is also optional.
- **Google Maps**: optional, for live drive-time estimates between in-person meetings.
- **A task tool or notes app**: optional, for audit context.
- **API keys:** none.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut.
2. The `agent-onboarding` skill runs before first use. It asks whose calendar this is, your hours and protected commitments, where alerts should land and which optional routines to turn on, then connects the accounts.
3. Ask for a supervised first audit of the next three business days, then let it set up the change trigger and the twice-daily schedule.

Re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

- Audit my next three business days and tell me what needs fixing
- Find my double-bookings this week and draft reschedule emails for them
- Keep my Open blocks synced to real free time for the next two weeks

## What's inside

- `AGENTS.md`: the four routines, Gamut mechanics, safe operating rules and the `## Your context` block.
- `.claude/skills/agent-onboarding/`: first-run setup, supervised dry run, triggers, schedules and `config.json`.
- `.claude/skills/calendar-checks/`: the issue rubric, collision priority order, alert fingerprinting, slot finding and placeholder rules.

## Notes

- Drafts only. Reschedule emails wait in your Drafts folder, and proposed slots are not held.
- Color-coding, open-time blocks and the slip alert are all off until you turn them on.
- If your calendar provider has no change trigger available, the agent checks every 10 minutes during waking hours instead.

## Privacy

The agent reads event details and, for the slip alert, calendar replies in the shared inbox. Slack posts include the meeting title, time and change, never email bodies or attachments. State files keep event IDs and alert fingerprints only, and old ones are pruned once events pass.

agents.details:
# Call Follow-Up Drafter

> Every client call ends with a follow-up already waiting in your drafts, in your voice, on the right thread.

## What it does

After each external call, Call Follow-Up Drafter reads the transcript, works out which client, engagement and email thread the call belongs to, and writes the follow-up you would have written: what you covered, the next steps you agreed (split into your side and theirs), and everything you asked the client for. The draft lands in your own Gmail or Outlook as a reply in the right conversation, addressed to the people who were on the call.

Getting the client right is the core rule. If a call mixes two clients, the client has more than one engagement, or the right thread isn't obvious, the agent asks you instead of guessing, and it never carries a name, number or detail from one client's call into another's email.

- **Per-call follow-up draft** — recap, next steps with owners and dates, and your asks, with numbers and dates quoted exactly as said.

- **Learns your voice** — from your sent mail and from the edits you make to its drafts.

agents.details:
# Call Follow-Up Nudge

> Walk out of every call knowing exactly what you promised, with the follow-ups already drafted.

## What it does

About thirty minutes after each call, Call Follow-Up Nudge reads the transcript and pulls out only what you personally agreed to: the deliverable, who it is for, and the deadline, with your exact words quoted. A passing "we should look at that" is not counted as yours, and what the other side took on goes in its own list.

It then drafts the follow-ups you promised as replies in the right thread in your own Gmail or Outlook, writes any promised Slack messages as copy-ready text, and sends you one message: your commitments at the top, the drafts below, and every "let me check and circle back" flagged so it does not quietly disappear.

- Numbers, prices, and dates are quoted exactly as said; any date it had to infer is marked as an estimate.
- Silent after calls where you promised nothing.
- Never processes the same call twice, whether the transcript arrives on time or an hour late.
- Optional daily check of what is due or overdue, or a hand-off to the Open Loops agent for long-running tracking.

Nothing is ever sent or posted as you.

## What you'll need

- **Google Calendar** — required (or Outlook), to find your calls and attendees.
- **Gmail or Outlook** — required, to save follow-up drafts in your mailbox and learn your tone from sent mail.
- **Granola** — or another notes source: Fathom, Fireflies, Otter, Gong, Zoom recordings, or inviting the agent to listen in on calls.
- **Slack** — optional, to address promised Slack messages to the right person and check whether you sent them.
- **A delivery channel** — the agent's own Slack app, its own email inbox, Telegram, iMessage, or in-app only, set up during onboarding.
- **API keys:** none.

3. It shadows one day of your real calls so you can correct what it caught before it runs on its own.

## Example prompts

agents.name: Chief of Staff Briefing
agents.description: Founder briefing across Gmail, Calendar, Slack, Discord and project tools: fires first, then decisions, meetings, commitments and open work.
agents.details:
# Chief of Staff Briefing

> A founder's early-morning briefing that puts the fires first, then everything only you can unblock.

## What it does

Every morning, before your day starts, the agent sweeps your Gmail, calendar, Slack, Discord and project tools since the last briefing. It ranks everything against your people tiers, the projects you care about and your own urgency rules.

The briefing leads with fires: what broke, which rule it tripped, who's already on it and what's needed from you. Then come the decisions and approvals waiting on you, today's meetings with what to prepare, commitments you owe and are owed, and one line per watched project that moved, slipped or went quiet. Anything you've handled or dismissed stays gone unless it changes.

Two optional extras: an hourly fire watch during working hours that alerts only on new fires, and an end-of-day pass with three short lists (where you're the blocker, replies people are waiting on, promises about to go stale) that stays silent when there's nothing.

## What you'll need

- **Gmail** — required; read for messages and your own commitments. Outlook works too.
- **Google Calendar** — required; read-only, for today's meetings.
- **Slack** — recommended; your account is read for DMs, mentions and the channels you choose.
- **Discord** — optional; read for the servers and channels you choose, usually through the agent's own Discord app in your server. Skipped if it can't read them.
- **Linear or another project tool** — optional (GitHub, Jira, Asana, Notion, ClickUp), for project movement.
- **A delivery channel** — optional; by default the briefing lands in its own chat in the app. It can also come as a DM from the agent's Slack app, an email from its own inbox, Telegram or iMessage.
- **API keys:** none.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut. The setup request is pre-filled in the message box from `PROMPT.md`; edit it if you like and send it.
2. Sending it starts the `agent-onboarding` skill. It connects your tools and asks for your people tiers, projects, channels and urgency rules, plus the briefing time, delivery and autonomy.
3. Review the supervised first briefing on real data, tune what counts as a fire, and let it schedule the daily run and any extras you turned on.

Re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

- Give me this morning's briefing with fires first
- What's waiting on my approval across Gmail and Slack right now?
- Turn on the end-of-day pass at 5:30pm and add an outage rule

## What's inside

- `PROMPT.md` — the setup request placed in your message box after import.
- `AGENTS.md` — the agent's instructions: morning briefing, fire watch, end-of-day pass, Gamut mechanics and safety rules.
- `.claude/skills/agent-onboarding/` — first-run setup, dry run and scheduling.
- `.claude/skills/fire-rules/` — the fire test, urgency-rule format, ranking and the dismissed-item ledger.

## Notes

- The agent reads and briefs on its own. Sending any message, changing your calendar, or any other external action waits for your approval. Reply drafts in your own mailbox are off unless you turn them on, and are never sent.
- If a source fails to load, the briefing says so at the top.
- For a lighter brief without fire-flagging, use Daily Briefing instead.

## Privacy

The agent reads your accounts through your own connections and keeps only IDs, dates, names and one-line summaries in its state files. The briefing goes only to you.

## Credits

Adapted from the original prompt by [@jessethanley](https://x.com/jessethanley) on [Bot Directory](https://botdirectory.ai/bots/chief-of-staff-briefing/), used under the MIT license; see the [attribution and license](../../sources/botdirectory/NOTICE.md).

agents.name: Daily Briefing
agents.description: Sends one two-minute workday brief: what needs you from email, Slack and open loops, plus today's calendar, ranked by consequence.
agents.details:
# Daily Briefing

> Start every workday knowing the five things that actually need you, in a message you can read in two minutes.

## What it does

Each workday morning, at the time you pick, the agent looks back at everything since your last brief (email, Slack, and any task tracker or meeting notes you connect) and ahead at today's calendar. It also checks your open loops: promises you made that are coming due, and things you're still waiting on from other people.

It ranks everything by consequence rather than arrival time, keeps a top handful under "Needs you today", and folds the rest into a count. Each meeting gets one line on who and why, with conflicts, unanswered invites and anything to prepare flagged. Monday's brief covers the weekend, and holidays and out-of-office days are skipped.

It remembers what you've handled or dismissed, so the same thread doesn't come back every morning unless something about it changed. On a quiet day you get one line instead of filler. If you like, it also makes a short audio version with the platform's built-in speech.

## What you'll need

- **Gmail or Outlook** — required; read-only, to find what needs you.
- **Google Calendar or Outlook Calendar** — required; read-only, for today's meetings and conflicts.
- **Slack** — recommended; your account is read for DMs, mentions and any channels you choose.
- **A task tracker or meeting notes** — optional (Todoist, Asana, Linear, Notion, Granola and others).
- **A delivery channel** — optional; a DM from the agent's own Slack app, an email from its own inbox, Telegram or iMessage. Otherwise the brief appears in the app.
- **API keys:** none. Audio uses built-in speech, metered per character; onboarding gives an estimate first.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut. The setup request is pre-filled in the message box from `PROMPT.md`; edit it if you like and send it.
2. Sending it starts the `agent-onboarding` skill. It connects your mail, calendar and Slack, asks who always matters and what to skip, and sets your time, workdays, delivery channel and audio preference.
3. Review the supervised first brief on real data, adjust, and let it schedule the daily run.

Re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

- Brief me now on what came in since yesterday morning
- What's due from me today, and who am I still waiting on?
- Move my brief to 7:30 on weekdays and add an audio version

## What's inside

- `PROMPT.md` — the setup request placed in your message box after import.
- `AGENTS.md` — the agent's instructions: the morning brief, dismissals, audio, Gamut mechanics and safety rules.
- `.claude/skills/agent-onboarding/` — first-run setup, dry run and scheduling.
- `.claude/skills/rank-and-remember/` — the consequence scoring and the ledger that stops handled items from resurfacing.

## Notes

- The agent is read-only. It never replies, accepts or declines invites, or changes anything in your mail, calendar or Slack.
- Reply "done 2", "drop 3" or "snooze the Acme one till Thursday" to tidy the brief.
- If a source fails to load, the brief says so instead of pretending it was a quiet day.
- Founders who want more sources, fire-flagging and an end-of-day pass should look at Chief of Staff Briefing instead.

## Privacy

The agent reads your mail, calendar and Slack through your own connected accounts. Its state files hold only IDs, dates, senders and one-line summaries, never message bodies.

## Credits

Adapted from the original prompt by [@elie2222](https://x.com/elie2222) on [Bot Directory](https://botdirectory.ai/bots/daily-briefing/), used under the MIT license; see the [attribution and license](../../sources/botdirectory/NOTICE.md).

agents.name: Deck Updater
agents.description: Turns each demo or discovery call into a tailored copy of your master deck, plus a covering email in your drafts, ready before the next meeting.
agents.details:
# Deck Updater

> Every demo ends with a deck about the prospect's problem, not your generic pitch, waiting in your Drive with the email already drafted.

## What it does

After each external demo or discovery call, Deck Updater reads the transcript and pulls out the prospect's goals, their pains in their own words, the use cases they cared about, the objections they raised, who was in the room, and the agreed next steps. It then copies your master Google Slides deck into a folder for that account and tailors the copy: a recap of the call, how you map to their top pains, proof points from your approved library, answers to their objections, pricing only if it came up, the agreed next steps, and one clear call to action. Slides that don't apply are cut; your theme, fonts and layouts are left alone.

Every tailored line is tagged in the speaker notes as said on the call or inferred, and you get a short review list of what to double-check. A covering email in your voice, linking the deck and naming the next step, waits in your Gmail drafts on the existing thread. If your next meeting with that account is already booked, the deck is ready before it, and a morning refresh picks up anything new from the thread.

Deck Updater never edits your master deck, never invents customer names, logos or numbers, never sends the email, and never shares the deck outside your company without your approval.

## What you'll need

- **Google Slides and Google Drive** — required. The master deck, the tailored copies and the per-account folders.
- **Gmail** — required for the covering-email drafts. Outlook works instead.
- **Google Calendar** — required, to find which sales calls ended and when the next one is.
- **Granola** — or another notes source: Gong, Fathom, Fireflies, Otter, Zoom recordings, or inviting the agent to listen in on calls.
- **HubSpot or Salesforce** — optional, read-only, for account context when picking calls.
- **A delivery channel** — the agent's own Slack app, its own email inbox, Telegram or iMessage for the "deck ready" notice. In-app only also works.
- **API keys:** none.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut and send the setup message that is already in the message box.
2. The `agent-onboarding` skill connects your tools, reads your master deck, maps your standard and proof-point slides, learns your email voice from sent mail, and asks how decks are named, shared and delivered.
3. It builds one supervised deck from a real recorded call so you can correct it, then sets up the transcript trigger or an hourly workday sweep.

Re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

- Build a follow-up deck from my last discovery call notes
- Tailor the master deck to the pains the Acme team raised and draft the email
- Refresh the deck before tomorrow's call with anything new from the thread

## What's inside

- `PROMPT.md` — the setup request placed in your message box after import.
- `AGENTS.md` — the post-call deck and pre-meeting refresh routines, Gamut mechanics, and safe operating rules.
- `.claude/skills/agent-onboarding/` — first-run setup that connects tools, maps the master deck, runs a supervised build, and schedules the work.
- `.claude/skills/slides-tailoring/` — how to copy and tailor the deck with the Slides API, the slide-library tags, the default outline, and the said-versus-inferred tagging.

## Notes

- Proof points come only from slides or a doc you mark as approved; anything missing shows up as a placeholder for you to fill.
- Decks stay private (or company-wide, if you choose). You decide when to share the link with the prospect.
- Pairs with Call Follow-Up Drafter (so the prospect gets one email, not two) and Forecast Notes Updater (the CRM note for the same call).

## Credits

Adapted from the original prompt by [@ericzakariasson](https://x.com/ericzakariasson) on [Bot Directory](https://botdirectory.ai/bots/deck-updater/), used under the MIT license; see the [attribution and license](../../sources/botdirectory/NOTICE.md).

# Desk Deputy

> One agent runs the whole front desk: inbox drafts, calendar moves, and a text back for every missed call.

## What it does

Desk Deputy is the one front-desk owner for micro-owners and founder-led SMBs that still run the desk themselves. It watches your inbox for customer, vendor, and is-this-spam mail and drafts replies in your voice. It books, reschedules, and reminds against your real calendar, offering only times that are actually free.

When a missed call or voicemail lands on the business line, it drafts a text back: we saw it, here is the next step. Inbox, calendar, and phone stay one job with one context instead of three workflows. Sends stay in draft until you approve, unless you pre-authorize a routine path during onboarding.

## What you'll need

- **Gmail** — required for the inbox and reply drafts.
- **Google Calendar** — required for booking, rescheduling, and reminders.
- **Slack** — required. Spicy exceptions and the daily desk summary land here.
- **OpenPhone** — optional, for missed calls and voicemail. No registry connector; connect the line during onboarding or forward voicemails to the inbox.
- **API keys:** none.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut.
2. The `agent-onboarding` skill runs before first use. It asks for your inbox, calendar, phone line, voice samples, and which sends may go out automatically, then saves the answers into `AGENTS.md` and `.claude/skills/agent-onboarding/config.json`.
3. Ask for the first run: Work today's inbox, calendar, and missed calls as one desk, drafting replies, invites, and texts without sending.

Re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

- Work today's inbox, calendar, and missed calls and show me the drafts
- Draft a text back to every voicemail from this morning with the next step
- Every weekday at 5pm, summarize the desk and what still needs my reply

## What's inside

## Notes

- Built for 1-15 person micro-owners and founder-led SMBs still running the desk themselves.
- The agent never answers legal, HR, or payment disputes on its own and never asks for passwords or 2FA codes in chat.
- It will not invent availability or hide a calendar conflict.

agents.name: Event Runner
agents.description: Runs a webinar or in-person event from run-up to follow-up: tracks readiness, drafts promo and reminders, then segments attendees and drafts follow-ups within a day.
agents.details:
# Event Runner

> Run your next webinar or event without dropping a ball, and follow up while the leads are still warm.

## What it does

Event Runner owns one event from the first promo to the last follow-up.

- **Run-up readiness.** Every morning until the event it checks the real state of things: promo beats sent, the registration page live with the right time, speakers confirmed in writing, slides and assets in, and reminders scheduled. It ranks what is at risk by how close the event is and splits it into "waiting on me" and "waiting on others". When the next promo or reminder is due, it drafts it for your approval.
- **Post-event follow-up.** Within a day of the event it pulls registrants and attendees from Eventbrite, Zoom, Luma, a sheet or your CRM. It sorts them into hand-raisers (attended and asked a question, answered a poll or clicked your CTA), attendees and no-shows, and drafts a personal follow-up for each. Hand-raisers get a reply to their actual question, and no-shows get the recording link.
- **Stops on its own.** Once the follow-up wave is drafted, the daily check cancels itself.

Every email, post and reminder is a held draft. Nothing goes out until you approve it.

## What you'll need

- **Gmail:** required. Drafts land in your own mailbox. Outlook works too.
- **Google Calendar:** required, for speaker invites and the event block.
- **Registration and attendance source:** Eventbrite or a Zoom webinar as connected accounts. Luma works through an API key if your calendar has API access, otherwise through its guest export. A Google Sheet or HubSpot list also works.
- **HubSpot:** optional, to flag existing deals and log engagement after approval. Salesforce, Attio, Pipedrive and Close also work.
- **Delivery channel:** in-app, or the agent's own Slack app, email inbox, Telegram or iMessage for daily readouts.
- **API keys:** only `LUMA_API_KEY`, and only if you use Luma's API.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut. The `agent-onboarding` skill starts automatically.
2. Onboarding records the event date, format, speakers and goal, and connects your mailbox, calendar and registration platform. It agrees the timeline and follow-up templates with you, then runs a first readiness check.
3. Approve the first promo or reminder draft, and let the daily readout and the post-event run take over.

Re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

- Track readiness for our Zoom webinar on December 3 and show what is at risk
- Pull last night's Eventbrite attendees and draft follow-ups by segment
- Draft the T-1 day reminder with the join link and hold it for me

## What's inside

- `AGENTS.md`: the run-up and post-event routines, Gamut mechanics, and safe operating rules.
- `.claude/skills/agent-onboarding/`: first-run setup, dry run, schedules, config and event record.
- `.claude/skills/event-playbook/`: the default readiness timeline, risk ranking, and segment and follow-up rules.

## Notes

- Zoom attendance, Q&A and poll reports depend on your Zoom plan. If one is not available, the agent asks for an export rather than guessing.
- The post-event run starts about two hours after the scheduled end, so reports and the recording have time to process. No-show drafts wait for a working recording link.
- For recurring community events synced into Notion and Slack, pair with `community-ops-crew`.

## Privacy

Event Runner reads registrant and attendee lists through your own connected accounts. Its state files keep only ids, segments and statuses. It never sends email or changes the event listing without your approval.

agents.name: Family Calendar Keeper
agents.description: Turns school, team and club mail into one shared family doc per kid, keeps the family calendar in sync, and warns early about pickup clashes.
agents.details:
# Family Calendar Keeper

> Every flyer, newsletter and last-minute pickup change becomes one shared plan the whole family can trust.

## What it does

Family Calendar Keeper reads mail only from the senders your family approves: teachers, the front office, coaches, clubs, class newsletters, school platforms and other parents. That includes schedules sent as PDFs, flyers and screenshots. It keeps one shared living doc organized per kid, with upcoming events, need-to-knows (forms, payments, RSVPs, "bring X", dress-up days, half-days) and what's due. New items go on top, and each one notes the email it came from.

The doc is the source of truth, and the agent keeps your family calendar matching it: it adds, updates and removes events and flags clashes. For the first week it asks before each calendar change; after that it syncs on its own and you can undo any change. Same-day changes, such as a moved pickup or a cancelled practice, reach you right away. Every early afternoon it checks today's and tomorrow's pickups and activities and tells you who's covering what and where you need a carpool or sitter. If a fix needs someone else to change plans, it drafts the message for you. It stays silent when the day is clean.

If you want them, it also sends ten at-home game ideas each week, tied to what the kids are learning and using only things you have. They come with a small printable pack for the car, and the agent remembers which games landed.

## What you'll need

- **Gmail**: required. It reads only the senders on your allowlist and keeps drafts. Outlook mail also works.
- **Google Calendar**: required, for the family calendar and the calendars it reads for pickups.
- **Google Docs and Google Drive**: required, for the shared family doc and sharing it with your partner, sitter or grandparents.
- **A way to reach you**: Telegram, iMessage, the agent's Slack app or its own email inbox, for urgent pings and digests.
- **Google Maps**: optional, for real drive times between schools and venues.
- **API keys:** none.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut.
2. The `agent-onboarding` skill runs before first use. It learns your kids and their activities, proposes a sender allowlist from your recent mail for you to approve, connects mail, calendar and docs, and picks where urgent pings go.
3. Ask it to build the family doc from this week's school mail and show the calendar changes it would make.

Re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

- Build our family doc from this week's school and team emails
- Check tomorrow's pickups and tell me if anything clashes
- Every Friday, send me ten games tied to what the kids learned this week

## What's inside

- `AGENTS.md`: the three routines, Gamut mechanics, safe operating rules and the `## Your context` block.
- `.claude/skills/agent-onboarding/`: first-run interview, allowlist builder, supervised dry run, schedules and `config.json`.
- `.claude/skills/family-doc-sync/`: the doc layout, item format, calendar reconcile rules, first-week approval mode and undo.

## Notes

- It never messages teachers, coaches, carpools or sitters, and it never pays, signs or RSVPs. Messages are drafts for you to send.
- It edits or removes only calendar events it created; events a person added are flagged, never changed.
- Different from `household-coordinator`, which is a daily household review built on Apple Messages and grades. The two can run side by side.

## Privacy

Only allowlisted senders are read; the rest of your inbox is never searched. The shared doc holds logistics only. Health, grades and custody details stay out of it unless you ask otherwise. The doc is shared only with the people you name, never by public link.

agents.description: Drafts the weekly cash update, runs the month-end close tracker, writes variance commentary and assembles the monthly board pack from your real numbers.
agents.details:
# Finance Reporting Desk

> The weekly cash note, the close checklist, the variance "why" and the board pack are ready before you sit down to write them.

## What it does

Finance Reporting Desk runs the recurring reporting work for a finance lead, controller, or founder acting as CFO:

- **Weekly cash update draft**: cash on hand, expected collections, upcoming payments, net burn and runway, then a short "what changed and why". It says so when a bank feed or sheet didn't refresh instead of guessing.
- **Month-end close tracker**: a living close-status doc built from your own checklist, covering unbooked invoices, accruals, deferred revenue, prepaids, missing receipts, bank recs and journal entries owed. It cross-checks your inbox for items that are sitting in email, marks something received only when it can see the evidence, ranks what's open by what blocks close and by amount, and drafts chase messages for your approval.
- **Monthly variance commentary**: only the 3-5 lines that matter against budget and forecast, with the "why" found in your email, Slack and notes. When it can't find a reason, it drafts a nudge to the budget owner instead of inventing one. It also flags data errors such as sign flips, missing months and doubled lines.
- **Board and investor reporting pack**: a four-period comparison table, the KPI read your board tracks, the variance narrative, and a "what to flag" section, saved as a dated doc.

It reads from QuickBooks or Xero, Stripe, Mercury, Ramp or Brex, and your budget and forecast sheets. It never posts to the books, moves money, or sends anything to anyone without your OK.

## What you'll need

- **QuickBooks** or **Xero**: your ledger, AR and AP. One of them is required, or regular exports.
- **Google Sheets** (or Excel): budget, forecast, close checklist and cash model.
- **Gmail** (or Outlook): inbox cross-checks during close, the "why" search, and drafts.
- **Stripe**: optional, for revenue, payouts and the clearing-account check.
- **Mercury**: optional, through its MCP server, for bank balances. Other banks work through a CSV drop or a browser session.
- **Ramp** or **Brex**: optional, through their MCP servers, for card balances and missing receipts.
- **Google Drive and Docs, Slack, Carta**: optional, for saved packs, the "why" search, report delivery, and stock comp.
- **API keys:** none.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut.
2. The `agent-onboarding` skill runs on first use. It asks which routines you want, where your numbers live, your close calendar and checklist, materiality, KPI definitions, and where drafts and reports should go. Then it connects your accounts and runs each routine once with you.
3. Ask for a first run: "Draft this week's cash update."

Re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

- Draft this week's cash update from Mercury and QuickBooks
- What's still open for the October close, and who are we waiting on?

agents.details:
# Forecast Notes Updater

> Walk into your forecast call with every opportunity already updated from what was actually said.

## What it does

After each customer call, demo or meaningful email exchange, Forecast Notes Updater reads the transcript, the thread and any Slack discussion about the deal, finds the right contact and opportunity, and drafts the note in your exact format and qualification framework. Gaps in your framework are called out, not filled in, and numbers and dates are quoted exactly as they were said.

It runs in the modes you choose:

- **Per-call updates** — as soon as a transcript is ready, a proposed note, next step and framework update for that deal. Each meeting is processed once.
- **End-of-day batch** — at 5pm, the day's calls, meetings and buyer emails drafted into one batch to approve, with duplicates of what is already logged removed.
- **Forecast-call digest** — optional: what changed on your in-play deals since last week, and what never got logged.

Stage and forecast changes are only suggested, each with the line from the call that supports it. The agent never moves a deal to closed lost or pass, never touches amounts or close dates on its own, and never overwrites a note a teammate edited later. For the first week it writes nothing without your approval; after that you can let it log plain notes on its own.

## What you'll need

- **Salesforce** — the primary CRM. HubSpot or Attio also work, and a Google Sheet if you have no CRM. Required, one of them.
- **Meeting notes** — Granola or Gong recommended. Fathom, Fireflies, Otter, Zoom recordings, or inviting the agent to listen in on calls also work.
- **Gmail or Outlook** — recommended, to read threads with buyers.
- **Google Calendar** — recommended, to know which meetings happened and who attended.
- **Slack** — optional, to read deal channels you allow.
- **A delivery channel** — the agent's own Slack app, its own email inbox, Telegram, or in-app only, for approval batches.
- **API keys:** none.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut and send the setup message that is already in the message box.
2. The `agent-onboarding` skill connects your CRM, notes, mail and calendar, asks for your note format, framework, stage rules and in-play deals, and picks the modes and delivery channel.
3. It runs on your last few calls and shows the proposed updates before writing anything.

Re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

- Draft the Salesforce update from my call with Example Co this morning
- Show me today's proposed CRM updates and write the ones I approve
- Every Monday before forecast, tell me what changed on my in-play deals

## What's inside

agents.name: Goals and Week Ahead
agents.description: Tracks company goals against target each week, explains every slip from real activity, drafts owner nudges for approval, and writes your week-ahead plan.
agents.details:
# Goals and Week Ahead

> Know which goals are slipping and why before your Monday meeting, and start every week with a plan instead of an inbox.

## What it does

Goals and Week Ahead reads each company goal from wherever its number really lives, whether a sheet, a CRM report, an analytics metric, or a Linear project, and judges it against the actual work behind it. Every Monday, or two hours before your leadership meeting, you get a one-page readout with at-risk goals first: current vs. target, week-over-week movement, owner, blocker, and the reason behind each slip. Reasons are drawn from Linear, Jira, and GitHub activity, email threads, and meeting notes, and each one cites its evidence.

For every slipping goal, it drafts a short, collegial nudge to the owner in your Gmail or Outlook for you to review. On Sunday evening it writes the coming week's plan into a living doc: your top three to five priorities tied to goals, what rolled over from last week, calendar notes such as overloaded days and focus blocks, and the conversations to have.

The readout is for your eyes only, and nothing is sent to anyone without you.

## What you'll need

- **Goal sources** — whatever holds each number: Google Sheets, Google Docs, Notion, HubSpot, Salesforce, Stripe, PostHog, and similar. Onboarding maps each goal to its source.
- **Linear** — recommended for work evidence. Jira, GitHub, or Asana also work.
- **Gmail** — required for owner status emails and nudge drafts. Outlook also works.
- **Google Calendar** — required for leadership meeting timing and the week-ahead calendar notes.
- **Google Docs** — for the week-ahead plan. Notion also works.
- **Meeting notes** — optional: Granola, Fathom, Fireflies, Otter, Gong, or Zoom.
- **API keys:** none for the common sources. A key-only metrics service can be added as a secret.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut.
2. The `agent-onboarding` skill runs before first use. You paste or point to your goals, and it walks through them one at a time to tie each to the source of its real number, its owner, its target, and how it should pace. Then it connects your work and calendar tools and picks where things land.
3. It builds this week's readout as a supervised dry run, so you can correct numbers, owners, and diagnoses before the weekly schedule starts.

Re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

- Map our Q4 goals to where each number actually lives
- Which goals are at risk this week, and why? Draft nudges to the owners
- Every Sunday at 6pm, draft my week-ahead plan in Google Docs

## What's inside

- `AGENTS.md` — the readout, owner nudges, and week-ahead routines, Gamut mechanics, and safe operating rules.
- `.claude/skills/agent-onboarding/` — first-run setup that builds the goal map, connects sources, sets schedules, and writes `config.json`.
- `.claude/skills/goal-status-rubric/` — pacing math, status thresholds for committed and stretch goals, and the named reasons for a slip with the evidence each needs.

## Notes

- A goal is never called off track on the number alone. The work behind it has to agree, and the evidence is linked.
- Stale or missing numbers are labeled as such, never carried forward or estimated.
- Each week's plan is a new section at the top of the doc, so your edits to earlier weeks are never overwritten.
- Pairs with Open Loops and Meeting Actions, which can feed open commitments and leadership decisions into the plan.

agents.description: Owns the weekly growth readout: a leadership update draft, what the website converts, and what is shifting in signups and pipeline.
agents.details:
# Growth Readout

> Start every Monday with the leadership update already drafted and a clear read on what your website and pipeline are really telling you.

## What it does

Every Monday morning Growth Readout pulls last week's numbers from whatever you have connected: Google Analytics, Search Console, Google Ads, product analytics, and your CRM. It compares them with the week before and with your recent baseline, then writes three things:

- **A leadership update draft**: headline takeaways, a compact numbers table with week-over-week changes, what changed and what it means, and your asks. It matches the format of a past update you share, and it always stays a draft.
- **A website section**: which pages and calls to action drive signups, which button copy is winning (and when it is too early to tell), where visitors stop scrolling on the homepage, and which traffic sources send people who convert, not just people who visit.
- **A "what's shifting" readout**: real changes in who is signing up and entering pipeline, such as a new industry or persona gaining traction, a channel bringing a different kind of lead, a use case catching on, or a segment going quiet. Each one comes with the evidence, what it might mean and a suggested next move. Normal weekly noise is filtered out.

A short summary goes to your team channel from the agent's own Slack app, and the full breakdown, with every table, lands in a shareable doc. Missing or broken data is called out by name, never reported as zero.

## What you'll need

- **Google Analytics 4**: recommended, for traffic, conversions, landing pages and scroll depth.
- **Google Search Console**: optional, for organic queries and pages.
- **Google Ads**: optional, for paid spend and conversions. Meta and LinkedIn ads are covered through a connection if one is offered, or a weekly export or sheet.
- **PostHog**: optional, for product events, experiments and heatmaps. Amplitude or Mixpanel work the same way.
- **HubSpot**: recommended, for leads and pipeline. Salesforce works too.
- **Google Docs**: recommended, for the full breakdown and the leadership draft. Markdown files are the fallback.
- **Slack**: optional, the agent's own Slack app posts the team summary. Email or in-app delivery work too.
- **API keys:** none.

The readout works with any subset of these sources and states clearly what is missing.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut.
2. The `agent-onboarding` skill runs on first use. It connects your sources, asks what counts as a signup, lead and pipeline, which segments matter, where the summary and doc should go, and when leadership needs the update. It also reads a past update to match your voice.
3. Ask for a dry run on last week's data, review it, then let the Monday schedule take over.

Re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

- Draft last week's marketing update from what's connected
- Which traffic sources actually converted to signups last week?
- What's shifting in our signups and pipeline versus the last two months?

## What's inside

- `AGENTS.md`: the three weekly routines, the data-honesty rules, the Gamut connections and schedule, and the `## Your context` block that onboarding fills in.
- `.claude/skills/agent-onboarding/`: first-run setup for sources, definitions, segments, delivery and the Monday schedule.
- `.claude/skills/shift-detection/`: the rules that separate a real signup or pipeline shift from weekly noise.

## Notes

- The agent reads only. It never changes ad accounts, analytics settings, experiments or CRM records, and never sends the leadership update.
- Ad-platform conversions are reported per platform and never added together, since each platform claims credit differently. The last few days of paid data are marked provisional.
- The first run backfills a baseline from your recent history when the sources allow it. Until then, shifts are described with less confidence.

# Handshake Closer

> Every verbal yes becomes a sent estimate, one nudge, and a clear flag when they go quiet.

## What it does

Handshake Closer owns the gap between a verbal yes and a sent estimate for micro-owners and founder-led SMBs. It watches notes, SMS, voicemail, and the inbox for a yes, a handshake, or a send-it-over, then drafts the estimate from your rate card or the number they already heard, plus a one-line scope.

If they go quiet after send, it drafts exactly one nudge after the wait you configure (default 3 days). If they are still silent after that, it Slacks you the file and stops. No seven-touch sequence, no fuzzy maybe treated as a yes, and no job marked won without a real yes on the sent estimate.

## What you'll need

- **Gmail** — required for catching yeses and drafting the estimate and nudge.
- **Slack** — required. Silence flags and exceptions land in your founder channel.
- **SMS line and estimate system** — optional. Connected during onboarding; no registry connector.

## Getting started

3. Ask for the first run: Find verbal yeses that still have no sent estimate, draft the estimates, and flag any silence after one nudge.

## Example prompts

agents.name: Important Email Triage
agents.description: Labels the mail genuinely waiting on your reply as it arrives, in your own categories, leaves ambiguous mail alone, and never sends, drafts or archives.
agents.details:
# Important Email Triage

> One label you can trust: everything a real person is waiting on you for, tagged within minutes of arriving.

## What it does

The agent watches your inbox as mail arrives (or every 30 minutes) and labels what's genuinely waiting on you: a question, a request, an approval, a deadline from a real person. Everything else goes into a handful of categories learned from your own mail and named the way you'd name them. Newsletters, receipts, notifications and cold outreach, including the fake "Re:" kind, are ignored.

When a message is ambiguous it leaves it alone instead of guessing, and it takes the label off once you've replied. When something new lands it sends you one short list, newest first, with who it is and what they're asking. No new labels means no message.

Investors can switch to a preset with four buckets (Today's Focus, Action Required, Scheduling, Delegated) and a one-line reason for every urgent item; a term sheet or signed document always goes to the top, and fund-admin mail stays out of deal flow.

## What you'll need

- **Gmail or Outlook** — required; the agent reads new mail and adds labels or categories.
- **A delivery channel** — optional; the agent's own Slack app, its own email inbox, Telegram or iMessage. You can also choose labels only.
- **API keys:** none.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut. The setup request is pre-filled in the message box from `PROMPT.md`; edit it if you like and send it.
2. Sending it starts the `agent-onboarding` skill: it connects your mailbox, learns who matters and which categories you use, and picks the delivery channel and hours.
3. Check the read-only dry run on your last two days of mail, then let it switch on the new-mail trigger or the 30-minute check.

Re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

- Label what's waiting on me in today's unread mail
- What is each person in my waiting label asking me for?
- Switch me to the investor buckets and flag any term sheets

## What's inside

- `PROMPT.md` — the setup request placed in your message box after import.
- `AGENTS.md` — the agent's instructions: labeling rules, the investor preset, triggers and safety rules.
- `.claude/skills/agent-onboarding/` — first-run setup, read-only dry run and trigger or schedule creation.
- `.claude/skills/triage-labels/` — the skip list, the waiting-on-me test, category learning and the processed-message ledger.

## Notes

- Labels only. It never sends, drafts, archives, deletes, marks read or unsubscribes. For cleanup and unsubscribes, use the Inbox Manager template; for daily reply drafts, use Inbox Reply Digest.
- All labels sit under one `Triage/` parent, so they are easy to find or remove.
- If your account offers no new-mail trigger, the agent checks every 30 minutes, optionally only during working hours.

## Credits

Adapted from the original prompt by [@elie2222](https://x.com/elie2222) on [Bot Directory](https://botdirectory.ai/bots/important-email-triage/), used under the MIT license; see the [attribution and license](../../sources/botdirectory/NOTICE.md).

agents.name: Inbox Manager
agents.description: Keeps your inbox sorted as mail arrives: labels it in your own categories, archives the noise, pre-drafts replies, and never sends.
agents.details:
# Inbox Manager

> Turn a noisy Gmail inbox into a short, useful queue of messages that deserve your attention.

## What it does

Inbox Manager sorts your mail in the background as it arrives. It learns your categories from your real mail and labels in your own words instead of a generic folder scheme, archives the noise you confirmed against a skip list, and leaves anything ambiguous exactly where it is. Each thread gets at most one label, and it never overrides a label you set yourself.

For threads that clearly need an answer from you, it writes a reply in your voice, learned from your sent mail, and leaves it in your Gmail drafts. It never sends. Once a week it tells you what you might not notice: senders you always ignore, threads you keep leaving hanging, and rules that keep misfiring. It proposes unsubscribes, and acts on one only after you approve that sender.

An optional investor preset swaps learned categories for four fixed buckets (Today's Focus, Action Required, Scheduling, Delegated), keeps LP and fund-admin mail out of deal flow, and sends a morning digest with a one-line reason for each urgent item.

## What you'll need

- **Gmail:** Required. Labels, archiving, drafts, and the bundled screening and unsubscribe tools all run through your connected Gmail account.
- **Outlook:** Optional alternative. The same work runs through Microsoft Graph, without the bundled Gmail scripts, so the first week runs in preview mode.
- **Google Calendar:** Optional, so scheduling drafts can offer real free times.
- **Slack, email, Telegram, or iMessage:** Optional, for summaries and the weekly report, sent from the agent's own account. In-app works too.
- **API keys:** None.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut.
2. The `agent-onboarding` skill runs before first use. It connects your mailbox, reads your recent mail to propose categories in your words, agrees the skip list and never-touch list with you, learns your voice from sent mail, and asks how much to do on its own.
3. Review the dry run on the last 48 hours of mail, nothing changed until you approve. Then it switches on sorting for new mail and the weekly patterns report.

Re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

- Sort today's unread and show me what you labeled, archived, and left alone
- Which senders do I always ignore, and which threads am I leaving hanging?
- Draft replies for the threads that need me today and leave them in Gmail

## What's inside

- `AGENTS.md` — the sorting, drafting, and patterns routines, the investor preset, Gamut setup, and safe operating rules.
- `.claude/skills/agent-onboarding/` — mailbox connection, category and voice learning, dry run, and trigger and schedule setup.
- `.claude/skills/gmail-inbox-screener/` — Gmail retrieval, first-pass marketing screening, and mark-read actions.
- `.claude/skills/gmail-unsubscribe/` — unsubscribe-link extraction for approved senders.

## Notes

- Default autonomy: it labels and archives on its own within your confirmed rules and writes drafts. It never sends, deletes, or marks mail as spam, and unsubscribes need your yes per sender.
- It runs on each new email through a new-mail trigger when your account offers one, otherwise as a sweep every 15 minutes during your waking hours.
- Gmail-first: the bundled scripts are Gmail-specific.

agents.details:
# Inbox Reply Digest

> One list each morning of every email and Slack thread someone is waiting on you for, with the replies already drafted.

## What it does

Once a day, at a time you pick, the agent reads your work email and your Slack DMs and mentions and keeps only the threads where a person is genuinely waiting on you: a direct question, a customer or prospect thread, a pricing or renewal question, an intro, a promise you haven't closed. It drops newsletters, notifications, receipts, calendar replies and internal noise, and skips threads where you replied last or someone else owns the next step.

Each item comes with a one-line reason, how long they've waited and a link, ordered by what's most time-sensitive or oldest. For email it saves a reply in your voice as a draft in your own mailbox; for Slack it gives you paste-ready text. On a day with nothing owed, it sends nothing.

It learns how you write from your sent mail, remembers what you've already handled so the same thread doesn't come back every morning, and never invents prices, dates or promises in a draft.

## What you'll need

- **Gmail or Outlook** — required; the agent reads your inbox and saves reply drafts there.
- **Slack** — recommended; your account is used read-only to find DMs and mentions that need a reply.
- **A delivery channel** — optional; the agent's own Slack app, its own email inbox, Telegram or iMessage. Otherwise the digest appears in the app.
- **API keys:** none.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut. The setup request is pre-filled in the message box from `PROMPT.md`; edit it if you like and send it.
2. Sending it starts the `agent-onboarding` skill: it connects your mailbox and Slack, learns your voice, asks who always matters and what to skip, and sets the time and delivery channel.
3. Review the supervised dry run on your last week of mail, adjust, and let it schedule the daily digest.

Re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

- What do I owe replies to from the last three days?
- Draft a reply to the pricing question from the Acme thread
- Run the digest every weekday at 8am and DM it to me on Slack

## What's inside

- `PROMPT.md` — the setup request placed in your message box after import.
- `AGENTS.md` — the agent's instructions: the daily digest, the voice refresh, Gamut mechanics and safety rules.
- `.claude/skills/agent-onboarding/` — first-run setup, dry run and scheduling.
- `.claude/skills/voice-profile/` — how the agent learns and applies your writing style.

## Notes

- The agent never sends a reply or posts in Slack as you. Email drafts wait in your mailbox; Slack suggestions are text in the digest, because Slack has no way to save a draft for you.
- It does not archive, label or mark anything read.
- Links point to the original message so you can clear the list in one pass.

## Privacy

The agent reads your mail and Slack messages through your own connected accounts. It keeps only thread IDs, dates and one-line reasons in its state files, plus a short style profile with no message bodies.

## Credits

Adapted from the original prompt by [@kristaletz](https://x.com/kristaletz) on [Bot Directory](https://botdirectory.ai/bots/inbox-reply-digest/), used under the MIT license; see the [attribution and license](../../sources/botdirectory/NOTICE.md).

agents.description: Owns inbound and prospect replies through a qualified call on the calendar: drafts each reply in your voice with real open times. Not a polite we-will-be-in-touch.
agents.details:
# Inquiry Desk

> Take every inbound inquiry all the way to a qualified call on your calendar, not a polite we-will-be-in-touch.

## What it does

Inquiry Desk owns inbound for founder-led consulting, accounting, insurance, and staffing firms. It watches the web form, email, and referral intros for new inquiries and scores each one against your fit rules: company size, problem, budget signal if they gave one, geography, and conflicts. For a fit, it reads your calendar, offers two or three real windows, and queues the invite for one-tap send. Poor fits get a polite, honest reply instead of a ghost.

It also catches prospects who reply to your outbound emails, and demo or consult requests. Within minutes of each one arriving, it drafts a reply in your voice, learned from your sent mail: short, direct, friendly, no filler. The reply answers what they actually asked and moves toward a booked call with real times from your calendar. A "not now" gets a gracious reply and a dated follow-up task, and a "no" is never argued with. Every reply stays in your Gmail drafts, and the agent never quotes fees unless a published rate is in config.

## What you'll need

- **Gmail** — required for inquiry intake, outbound replies, your writing voice, and reply drafts. Outlook works too.
- **Google Calendar** — required to offer real windows and book the call.
- **HubSpot** — the supported CRM connector for logging inquiries. Another CRM can be configured during onboarding.
- **Slack** — for alerts on new qualified leads and drafts waiting, sent from the agent's own Slack app. Email or in-app also work.
- **API keys:** none.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut.
2. The `agent-onboarding` skill runs before first use. It asks for your inquiry sources, how to spot your outbound threads, your fit rules, who takes the call, which calendar to book against, and where alerts go. It reads your sent mail to learn your voice, then saves the answers into `AGENTS.md` and `.claude/skills/agent-onboarding/config.json`.
3. Ask for the first run: Work today's inbound inquiries through a qualified call on the calendar, drafting invites for approval. After you approve, it sets up the new-mail trigger.

Re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

- Work today's inbound inquiries and draft invites for the qualified ones
- Draft replies to the prospects who answered my outreach this week
- On every new inquiry, draft my reply with three open times and Slack me

## What's inside

- `AGENTS.md` — the inbound and prospect reply routines, reply types and voice rules, the Gamut setup, safe operating rules, and the `## Your context` block that onboarding fills in.
- `.claude/skills/agent-onboarding/` — the first-run interview that captures your systems, fit rules, voice, and booking rules, runs a supervised drafting pass, and sets up the trigger.

## Notes

- Built for 2-200 person founder-led professional firms with inbound sitting in the inbox.
- Every reply is a draft for your review. The agent never sends, never books a time the calendar does not show, and never stops at a qualified-lead list without offering a call.

agents.name: Investor Update Drafter
agents.description: Drafts the recurring investor, LP or partner update from what actually happened, picking up where the last one left off. Never sends.
agents.details:
# Investor Update Drafter

> Your monthly update is 90% written before you remember it's due, and it never forgets what you promised last time.

## What it does

Investor Update Drafter starts from the last update you actually sent, found in your sent mail or a Drive folder. It lists the metrics you reported, the asks you made, and every "next period" commitment. Then it gathers what changed: what shipped in GitHub and Linear, revenue from Stripe, numbers from your metrics sheet, hires, fundraising and pipeline movement, customer wins, and the risks your team raised internally.

It drafts in your voice and your structure. The headline comes first, metrics are stated against last period, every old commitment is marked done, in progress or dropped with a reason, and the asks are specific enough to act on. When it can't find or reconcile a number, it writes "(needs number)" and lists every gap in a short summary. If a draft already exists for the period, or nothing material changed, it skips and tells you why.

It works for a founder's monthly update, an LP letter, or a partner-meeting recap. An EA or chief of staff can also use it to draft for a principal. The draft lands in your Gmail drafts or a Google Doc. It never sends.

## What you'll need

- **Gmail** (or Outlook): required. Finds your last update and saves the new draft in your own mailbox.
- **Google Drive**: needed if past updates or the output live in Drive. Google Docs is used when the draft should be a Doc.
- **Google Sheets**: optional, for a metrics sheet. Excel works too.
- **Stripe**: optional, for revenue and subscription metrics.
- **Linear** and **GitHub**: optional, for what shipped this period.
- **PostHog, Amplitude or Mixpanel**: optional, through their MCP servers, for product metrics.
- **A CRM** (HubSpot, Salesforce or Attio): optional, for pipeline and customer wins.
- **API keys:** none.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut.
2. The `agent-onboarding` skill runs on first use. It asks whether you send the update or draft it for someone, what kind of update it is and when it's due, where past updates and your numbers live, and where the draft and summary should land. Then it connects those accounts and runs one supervised draft with you.
3. Ask for your first draft: "Draft this month's investor update from last month's."

Re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

- Draft this month's investor update starting from the one I sent last month
- What did I promise investors last update, and where does each one stand?
- Every month, draft my update 3 days before the 5th and leave it in Gmail

## What's inside

- `AGENTS.md`: the drafting routine, the details that keep updates honest, connection and scheduling mechanics, and safe operating rules.
- `.claude/skills/agent-onboarding/`: first-run setup that writes `config.json` and creates the schedule.
- `.claude/skills/update-structure/`: the default update structure, LP and partner-recap variants, and the pre-handoff checklist.

## Notes

- It only drafts. Sending, adding recipients, and sharing the doc are always up to you.
- It never invents numbers, and it never computes fund performance figures for LP letters. Missing values stay as visible placeholders.
- Run state lives in `/workspace/state/` (which periods were drafted, and the running commitments list).

## Privacy

The agent reads your sent mail, drafts, and the sources you connect, only to build the update. Anything sensitive, such as customers under NDA, people matters or round terms, is flagged for your decision rather than written into the draft.

agents.name: Invoice Ask
agents.description: Owns customers who owe you: keeps a simple aging log and drafts a founder-voice ask on cadence until paid or escalated. Opposite of Vendor Nudge.
agents.details:
# Invoice Ask

> Ask the customers who owe you, on cadence and in your voice, until they pay or you step in.

## What it does

Invoice Ask owns customers who owe you for micro-owners and founder-led SMBs. Twice a week it pulls open customer invoices from QuickBooks, Xero, Stripe or your invoice sheet, buckets them as current, 1-30, 31-60 and 60+ days past due, and keeps a simple aging log of who owes what and when you last asked.

For each overdue customer it drafts one short ask per cycle in your voice, light at first and more direct as it ages, naming the invoice number, amount and due date. It skips anyone paid, on a payment plan or inside a promise date, and it only counts an invoice as paid once the money has cleared. "I sent it" is logged as a claim, and Venmo, Zelle or cash payments you took off the books are checked with you before anyone gets asked.

Replies are read as they arrive, promises are watched, and after the last unanswered ask you get a message from the agent with a suggested next step and a worst-offenders summary. Vendor bills stay out of this queue entirely; that is Vendor Nudge's job.

It is the simplest of the receivables agents: Invoice Hunter is tuned for trades jobs, Ledger Hawk for professional firms that also need invoices drafted, and Billing Chaser for agencies with unbilled time and retainers.

## What you'll need

- **QuickBooks, Xero, Stripe or a Google Sheet** — one is required for open customer invoices.
- **Gmail or Outlook** — required. Asks are drafts in your own mailbox and replies are watched there.
- **Slack, email, Telegram or iMessage** — the agent messages you from its own account, set up during onboarding. In-app works too.
- **Square, Wave or FreshBooks** — optional. No registry connector; an API key, a browser sign-in, or an export.
- **API keys:** none required.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut.
2. The `agent-onboarding` skill runs before first use. It connects your invoice source and mailbox, asks for your cadence, voice, off-book payment habits and do-not-ask customers, runs a supervised first ask cycle, and schedules the cycle and the reply watch.
3. Ask for the first run: list customers who owe you and draft the next asks, without sending.

Re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

- List who owes us and draft the next ask for each open invoice
- Draft a second ask for the Bell Plumbing invoice that is 20 days late
- Who has said they paid but nothing has cleared yet?

## What's inside

- `AGENTS.md` — the routines (ask cycle, promises and replies, escalation and recap), the Gamut mechanics, safe operating rules, and the `## Your context` block that onboarding fills in.
- `.claude/skills/agent-onboarding/` — the first-run setup: connections, questions, supervised dry run, schedules and triggers, and `config.json`.
- `.claude/skills/collections-playbook/` — aging buckets, the aging log format, the tone ladder, the cleared-payment test, skip rules and the one-ask-per-cycle ledger.

## Notes

- Built for 1-15 person micro-owners who know who owes them and still have not asked.
- Asks stay in draft until you send them. This agent is the opposite of Vendor Nudge and never chases vendors or pays bills.
