agents.description: Owns overdue job invoices for home services shops: aging log, escalating chase drafts, promise-to-pay tracking and founder handoff.
agents.details:
# Invoice Hunter

> Chase every overdue invoice through reminder, promise-to-pay, and human handoff instead of watching an aging report grow.

## What it does

Invoice Hunter owns overdue job invoices for founder-led home services shops. Twice a week it pulls open invoices from QuickBooks or Xero, buckets them as current, 1-30, 31-60 and 60+ days past due, and keeps a living aging log of who owes what, how overdue, and when you last reached out.

For each overdue account it drafts one reminder per cycle in your shop voice, firmer as the invoice ages, naming the invoice number, job, amount and due date. It skips anyone paid, on a payment plan, inside a promise date, or with an open callback, and it only counts an invoice as paid once the money has cleared. "Check's in the mail" is logged as a claim, not a payment.

Customer replies are read as they arrive: promises are logged and watched, disputes go to you. Accounts past your handoff age reach your founder channel from the agent's own Slack app with the file and a recommended next step, plus a worst-offenders summary each cycle. Every reminder stays a draft in your mailbox until you approve it.

It differs from Invoice Ask (micro-owners, no vertical), Ledger Hawk (professional firms, also invoices completed work) and Billing Chaser (agencies, also unbilled time and retainers) by focusing on trades jobs: homeowners, property managers, GCs and callbacks.

## What you'll need

- **QuickBooks or Xero** — one is required for open invoices and payment status.
- **Stripe** — optional, for card payments and hosted payment links.
- **Gmail or Outlook** — required. Reminder drafts land in your own mailbox and customer replies are watched there.
- **Slack** — the agent posts escalations from its own Slack app, set up during onboarding. Your own Slack account is only needed if it should read a payments channel.
- **Jobber, Housecall Pro or ServiceTitan** — optional, for job context. No registry connector; an API key, a browser sign-in, or a sheet export.
- **Google Sheets** — optional, if you want the aging log as a sheet.

## Getting started

2. The `agent-onboarding` skill runs before first use. It connects your books and mailbox, asks for your aging buckets, grace days, chase cycle, voice, handoff rule and do-not-chase customers, runs a supervised first chase on real data, and schedules the cycle and the reply watch.
3. Ask for the first run: pull overdue invoices, draft the next chase, and flag anything that needs you, without sending.

## Example prompts

agents.name: Ledger Hawk
agents.description: Owns invoices out the door and overdue chased for professional firms: drafts invoices for completed work, keeps the aging log, and drafts escalating chases.
agents.details:
# Ledger Hawk

> Completed work gets invoiced and overdue invoices get chased, in your voice, until they are paid or you step in.

## What it does

Ledger Hawk owns invoices out and overdue chased for founder-led consulting, accounting, insurance, staffing and law firms. Each week it finds completed work, approved time, retainer periods and placements with no invoice yet, and drafts the invoice in QuickBooks or Xero with the right terms, PO number and billing contact. Clients who only pay through an AP portal are flagged on the draft.

Twice a week it buckets open invoices as current, 1-30, 31-60 and 60+ days past due, keeps a living aging log, and drafts one chase per client per cycle, firmer as it ages, naming the invoice number, amount and due date. Paid accounts and payment plans are skipped, and an invoice counts as paid only once the money has cleared. "Payment is scheduled" is logged as a claim, not a payment.

Client replies and bounces are read as they arrive. Accounts past your handoff age reach you from the agent's own Slack app with the file, a recommended next step, and a worst-offenders summary. Invoices and chases stay in draft until you approve them.

Unlike Invoice Hunter (trades jobs) and Invoice Ask (simple chasing, no vertical), it also gets completed work billed; unlike Billing Chaser (agencies), it does not reconstruct time or manage retainer burn.

## What you'll need

- **QuickBooks or Xero** — one is required for unbilled work, open invoices, payments and invoice drafts.
- **HubSpot** — recommended for completed deals and billing contacts. Salesforce or Attio work as alternatives.
- **Gmail or Outlook** — required. Invoice covers and chases land as drafts in your mailbox.
- **Slack** — the agent posts escalations from its own Slack app, set up during onboarding. Your own Slack account is only needed if it should read a billing channel.
- **Stripe** — optional, if clients pay by card or ACH there.
- **Harvest, Toggl or a timesheet** — optional, for hourly billing. Harvest and Toggl connect with an API key.
- **API keys:** only for Harvest or Toggl, if you use them.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut.
2. The `agent-onboarding` skill runs before first use. It connects your books, CRM and mailbox, asks for your terms, PO and portal clients, aging, chase cycle, voice and handoff rule, runs a supervised first pass, and schedules billing, collections and the reply watch.
3. Ask for the first run: draft invoices for completed unbilled work and the next overdue chases, without sending.

Re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

- Draft invoices for completed unbilled work and the next overdue chases
- Show me everything over 45 days and draft a firmer chase for each
- Which clients said payment is scheduled but nothing has cleared?

## What's inside

- `AGENTS.md` — the routines (ready to bill, collections cycle, replies and promises, escalation and recap), the Gamut mechanics, safe operating rules, and the `## Your context` block that onboarding fills in.
- `.claude/skills/agent-onboarding/` — the first-run setup: connections, questions, supervised dry run, schedules and triggers, and `config.json`.
- `.claude/skills/collections-playbook/` — aging buckets, the aging log format, the tone ladder, the cleared-payment test, skip rules and the one-chase-per-cycle ledger.

## Notes

- Built for 2-200 person founder-led professional firms with completed work unbilled and overdue sitting.
- Invoices and chases stay in draft until the founder sends. The agent never touches client trust funds, never logs into client AP portals, and never writes legal or collections language.

agents.name: Meeting Actions
agents.description: Turns internal, leadership, and client meetings into decisions, owned and dated tasks in your tracker, routed hand-offs, and a running decisions log.
agents.details:
# Meeting Actions

> Every meeting ends with owners, due dates, and tasks already filed, and nothing agreed in the room gets lost by Friday.

## What it does

Meeting Actions reads the transcript of each team, staff, leadership, or client-delivery meeting and pulls out three things: decisions, action items with an owner and a due date, and open questions. Estimated dates are labeled. Owners are matched against the attendee list, and anything ambiguous comes back to you to confirm instead of being guessed.

It then does the admin you would otherwise do by hand:

- **Files tasks** in Linear, Jira, Asana, Monday, Todoist, Notion, GitHub Issues, or a Google Sheet. Tasks are filed as you, or as the agent's own Linear or GitHub app if you prefer automated work to be visibly labeled. It checks for an existing task before creating one, so the same commitment raised in three meetings is still one task.
- **Routes the pieces**: product feedback to the product channel, a customer ask to the account owner. Internal posts come from the agent's own Slack app, and anything external waits as a draft in your Gmail or Outlook.
- **Keeps a leadership decisions log**, newest first, that flags reversals of earlier decisions and carries open follow-through items into the next meeting.
- **Logs client next steps** against the right client and engagement, and never blends two clients together.

Sales and client close-out calls belong to Call Closer and Call Follow-Up Drafter. This template is for the meetings where your own team decides and divides work.

## What you'll need

- **Google Calendar** — required, to find meetings, attendees, and your recurring leadership series. Outlook calendar also works.
- **Granola** — or another transcript source: Fathom, Fireflies, Otter, Gong, Zoom recordings, or the agent joining the call in listen mode.
- **Linear** — or your tracker of choice: Jira, Asana, Monday, Todoist, Notion, GitHub Issues, or a Google Sheet.
- **Gmail** — recommended, for group follow-up and external drafts. Outlook also works.
- **Google Docs** — for the decisions log. Notion or a Google Sheet also works.
- **Slack** — optional. The agent's own Slack app posts routed items to channels and teammates.
- **API keys:** none.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut.
2. The `agent-onboarding` skill runs before first use. It connects your calendar, transcripts, and tracker, maps attendees to tracker users and topics to channels, sets up your client domains and decisions log, and asks how much the agent may do alone.
3. It processes your most recent meeting as a supervised dry run, creating nothing until you approve, then sets up a transcript-ready trigger or an hourly workday sweep.

Re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

- Pull the action items from this morning's staff meeting and show me
- File Linear issues for every action item from Tuesday's leadership sync
- What did leadership decide this month, and what reversed?

## What's inside

- `AGENTS.md` — the three routines, the filing-identity tradeoff, the no-duplicates rule, Gamut mechanics, and safe operating rules.
- `.claude/skills/agent-onboarding/` — first-run setup that connects tools, builds the people, routing, and client maps, and writes `config.json`.
- `.claude/skills/meeting-ledger/` — extraction rules, owner resolution, task fingerprinting and tracker search, the recap layout, and the decisions-log format.

## Notes

- Each meeting is processed exactly once. Where your transcript tool has no "transcript ready" event, an hourly workday sweep picks meetings up 30 minutes after they end.
- For the first three meetings, the agent shows its work and asks before filing or posting. External messages are always drafts.
- Pairs with Open Loops, which can receive each meeting's delegations and chase them.

## Privacy

Transcripts are read through your own connected accounts. Sensitive topics such as compensation, performance, and legal matters are never routed to channels. If the agent joins a call to listen, every attendee can see it in the participant list.

agents.details:
# Meeting Prep Brief

> Walk into every outside call knowing who is in the room, what you promised last time, and the one thing to ask.

## What it does

Meeting Prep Brief reads your calendar, skips internal meetings by attendee email domain, and writes one short, phone-friendly brief for each external, first-time or high-stakes meeting. Each brief leads with the one thing to say or ask, then who is in the room, your email history with them, what each side promised last time (open items first), what has changed since you last spoke, and recent company news with dates and links.

- **Depth by meeting type**: a first meeting gets the full who-are-they picture; a routine check-in gets only what changed and what is open.
- **Your timing**: one message the evening before, or a brief per meeting shortly before each call.
- **Optional enrichments**: call notes from Granola or Gong, the deal record from Salesforce, HubSpot or Attio, and internal Slack chatter about the account.
- **Optional deck**: if you have a slides agent in your workspace, it can ask that agent for a tailored deck, with your OK.
- **Read-only**: it never contacts attendees, never touches your calendar, and never sends anything as you.

## What you'll need

- **Google Calendar or Outlook** — required, to find the meetings worth briefing.
- **Gmail or Outlook mail** — required, for history with each attendee and past promises.
- **Granola, Gong, Fireflies, Otter or Fathom** — optional, for what was said and promised on past calls.
- **Salesforce, HubSpot or Attio** — optional, for stage, amount and next step.
- **Slack** — optional, for internal chatter about the account; also an optional delivery channel through the agent's own Slack app.
- **API keys:** none. Web research and people lookups use built-in search and enrichment.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut. The setup request is pre-filled in the message box from `PROMPT.md`; edit it if you like and send it.
2. Sending it starts the `agent-onboarding` skill: it connects your calendar and mail, asks which domains are internal, which meetings count, when to deliver and where, then writes a supervised brief for a real upcoming meeting.
3. Once you approve the brief, it schedules the planning runs and briefs land on their own.

Re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

- Prep me for my next external meeting on Google Calendar
- What did we promise the Acme team on our last Gong call?
- Brief every first-time call 45 minutes before it starts

## What's inside

- `PROMPT.md` — the editable setup request placed in your message box after import.
- `AGENTS.md` — the agent's routines, research rules, Gamut mechanics and safe operating rules.
- `.claude/skills/agent-onboarding/` — first-run setup, dry run and scheduling.
- `.claude/skills/meeting-triage/` — which meetings get a brief, the depth for each meeting type, and the brief format.

## Notes

- LinkedIn is read through search-result snippets, not by opening profile pages, so some titles may be missing or flagged as unconfirmed.

agents.details:
# Nutrition Agent

> Track calories, macros, and body weight with fast meal logging, a visual dashboard, and smart goal setting.

## What it does

A personal nutrition tracker you can message naturally. Describe what you ate (or send a photo), and the agent estimates macros and logs it. It tracks daily calories, protein, fat, and carbs against your goal, logs body weight over time, and gives you a beautiful dashboard to see trends. It can also research restaurant dishes before you order.

## What you'll need

- **Accounts:** None required. Optionally connect Telegram for on-the-go logging.
- **API keys:** None.

## Getting started

1. Import this template into Gamut.
2. On import, a setup session starts automatically. The **agent-onboarding** skill will:
   - Ask your name
   - Collect body metrics (sex, age, height, weight, activity level)
   - Calculate your TDEE and propose daily calorie + macro targets
   - Log your baseline weight
   - Ask about coffee/logging preferences
   - Optionally connect Telegram so you can log meals from your phone
3. Once setup finishes, just tell the agent what you ate!

You can re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

- I had a chicken burrito bowl and a cold brew
- How am I tracking against my calorie and protein goal?
- Log my weight and show me the last month's trend

## What's inside

- `AGENTS.md` — the agent's instructions (logging style, response format).
- `.claude/skills/agent-onboarding/` — first-run setup: TDEE interview, goal setting, Telegram connection.
- `.claude/skills/log-meal/` — log food from description or photo.
- `.claude/skills/log-weight/` — record daily body weight.
- `.claude/skills/edit-meal/` — fix or delete a logged meal.
- `.claude/skills/nutrition-status/` — generate Apple-Fitness-style progress ring PNG.
- `.claude/skills/nutrition-dashboard/` — open the interactive web dashboard.
- `.claude/skills/research-food/` — look up restaurant dish nutrition before ordering.
- `.claude/skills/set-nutrition-goal/` — recalculate TDEE and update goals anytime.
- `nutrition/` — Python scripts, SQLite database, and meal cheatsheet.
- `artifacts/nutrition-dashboard/` — Bun-based dashboard (calories, macros, weight charts, meal history).
- `nutrition/data/nutrition.db` + `nutrition/data/nutrition.db.bootstrap.sql` — empty database and schema.

## Notes

- All day boundaries use **America/Los_Angeles** (PST/PDT).
- The agent estimates macros from food descriptions and photos — it's not a precision scale, but it's consistent and fast.
- The cheatsheet (`nutrition/cheatsheet.md`) builds up over time with dishes you eat often, so estimates get faster and more accurate.
- To reset everything, delete `nutrition/data/nutrition.db` and re-run `uv run nutrition/scripts/init_db.py`.

agents.details:
# One-On-One Prep

> Walk into every standing 1:1 with last week's open items, their pending asks, and your agenda already on the page.

## What it does

One-On-One Prep keeps a private running doc for each recurring 1:1, whether with your manager, your reports, peers or clients. A couple of hours before each one, it adds a new dated section on top: what each of you still owes from last time (carried forward until there is evidence it was done), what the person has emailed or messaged you about since, the decisions or approvals they are waiting on from you, the topics you flagged during the week, a short suggested agenda, and space for your own talking points.

- **Every recurring 1:1**: found from your calendar and confirmed by you, with the agenda order tuned to the relationship.
- **Running thread, not a blank page**: items that keep slipping are marked by week and pushed up the agenda.
- **Topics on the fly**: tell the agent "for my 1:1 with Sam, raise the hiring plan", or type into the box at the top of the doc.
- **Optional reminders**: for what you promised, after each 1:1.
- **Private by design**: the doc is never shared with the other person and nothing is posted where they can see it.

## What you'll need

- **Google Calendar or Outlook** — required, to find your recurring 1:1s.
- **Gmail or Outlook mail** — recommended, for recent asks and proof that items were done.
- **Granola** — recommended, for what was said last time; Fireflies, Otter, Fathom or Zoom notes also work.
- **Slack** — optional, to include your DMs and mentions with each person; also an optional heads-up channel through the agent's own Slack app.
- **Google Docs** — optional home for the running docs; Notion or a Markdown file in the agent also work.
- **API keys:** none.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut. The setup request is pre-filled in the message box from `PROMPT.md`; edit it if you like and send it.
2. Sending it starts the `agent-onboarding` skill: it connects your calendar and notes, lists your recurring 1:1s for you to confirm, asks the relationship for each, and preps your next 1:1 with you watching.
3. Once you approve the first doc, it schedules the daily planning run and preps land on their own.

Re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

- Prep my next 1:1 from Google Calendar and show me the doc
- For my 1:1 with my manager, raise the Q1 hiring plan
- Before every recurring 1:1, carry forward what Granola says is open

## What's inside

- `PROMPT.md` — the editable setup request placed in your message box after import.

## Notes

- An item is only marked done when there is evidence, such as a sent email, a shared doc or a closed ticket; anything you tick yourself in the doc wins.

agents.name: Open Loops
agents.description: Tracks what you promised and what you handed off, closes each loop only on evidence, and drafts the nudges for your approval.
agents.details:
# Open Loops

> Every promise you make and every task you hand off stays on one list until there is proof it got done.

## What it does

Open Loops keeps a single ledger of what you owe people and what people owe you, harvested from your sent mail, your Slack messages, and your meeting notes. It tells a real commitment ("I'll send the revised SOW Thursday") from passing talk ("we should revisit pricing"), and it closes a loop only when it finds evidence: the email with the attachment, the intro with both people on it, the calendar invite.

It runs as four routines you can switch on separately:

- **End-of-day can't-miss sweep** — before you log off: where you are the blocker, replies you owe, and promises due by tomorrow morning. Silent when there is nothing.
- **Weekly promise sweep** — every open promise from the week, grouped by person or client, with the source linked.
- **Delegation chaser** — what you handed off and never got back, split into "their court" and "waiting on you", with a polite nudge drafted in the original thread for each overdue item.
- **Principal mode** — for executive assistants and chiefs of staff: commitments made by you, by your executive, and to your executive, ranked by who they are owed to.

Nudges are saved as drafts in your own Gmail or Outlook. Nothing is ever sent in your name.

## What you'll need

- **Gmail or Outlook** — required. Reads sent and received mail and saves nudge drafts in your mailbox.
- **Google Calendar** — recommended, to confirm "I'll set up a call" promises and respect out-of-office time.
- **Slack** — optional. Reads your own messages, DMs, and mentions for promises and asks.
- **Granola** — optional, for spoken commitments. Fathom, Fireflies, Otter, Gong, Zoom recordings, or inviting the agent to listen in on calls also work.
- **A delivery channel** — the agent's own Slack app, its own email inbox, Telegram, or iMessage, set up during onboarding. In-app only also works.
- **API keys:** none.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut.
2. The `agent-onboarding` skill runs before first use. It connects your mail, calendar, Slack, and notes, asks who your VIPs and clients are, which routines to turn on and when, and where digests should reach you.
3. It then runs a supervised sweep over your last two weeks so you can correct what it caught before anything is scheduled.

Re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

- Show me every promise I made in email in the last two weeks
- What have I delegated that went quiet? Draft the nudges in Gmail
- Every weekday at 4:30pm, tell me only what can't wait until tomorrow

## What's inside

- `AGENTS.md` — the four routines, the evidence rules for closing a loop, Gamut mechanics, and safe operating rules.
- `.claude/skills/agent-onboarding/` — first-run setup that connects tools, sets schedules, and writes `config.json`.
- `.claude/skills/commitment-ledger/` — how to classify, dedupe, date, rank, and close loops, and the ledger file format.

## Notes

- The ledger lives in the agent's workspace under `state/open-loops/` and stores one-line summaries and links, not message bodies.
- Slack has no draft API for your account, so Slack nudges arrive as copy-ready text in the digest.
- Pairs with Meeting Actions, which can hand each meeting's delegations straight into the ledger.

## Privacy

Open Loops reads your mailbox, calendar, Slack, and meeting notes through your own connected accounts. Digests go only to you. In principal mode, your executive's mail is read only if you already have delegated access, and only summaries and links are kept.

agents.details:
# OpenSlide Studio Agent

> Create, edit, preview, and present polished slide decks in a native Gamut-managed OpenSlide dashboard.

## What it does

This template provides a slide-focused agent and a fully wired OpenSlide dashboard. The dashboard artifact is the OpenSlide project itself, so Gamut installs the real dependencies with Bun before starting it. The library supports deck search, native editing and presentation views, deep routes, and live updates through Vite HMR.

The stock **Getting Started** deck is included so the studio is useful immediately after import.

## What you'll need

- **Accounts:** None.
- **API keys:** None.
- **Other:** A Gamut environment with dashboard artifacts enabled and package-registry access for the first automatic Bun install.

## Getting started

1. Import this template zip into Gamut.
2. Open the **OpenSlide Studio** dashboard.
3. Gamut discovers `artifacts/open-slide-studio/package.json`, installs the locked dependencies with Bun, and launches OpenSlide.
4. Browse the stock Getting Started deck or ask the agent: `Create a slide deck about …`
5. Saved deck edits update in the open dashboard through native HMR; no restart is needed.

No onboarding session is required because this template has no user-specific settings, accounts, databases, or secrets.

## Example prompts

- Build me a six-slide deck on our Q3 roadmap
- Restyle this deck with a cleaner theme
- Open the deck library and present the launch deck

## What's inside

- `AGENTS.md` — the slide agent's durable role, native dashboard contract, commands, and skill map.
- `artifacts/open-slide-studio/` — the complete OpenSlide application and dashboard artifact.
- `artifacts/open-slide-studio/package.json` — real dependencies, scripts, and `gamut.upstreamPath: mounted`.
- `artifacts/open-slide-studio/bun.lock` — dependency lockfile used by Gamut's automatic installer.
- `artifacts/open-slide-studio/open-slide.config.ts` — reads `DASHBOARD_BASE_PATH` and `DASHBOARD_PORT`.
- `artifacts/open-slide-studio/slides/getting-started/` — OpenSlide's stock sample deck and assets.
- `.claude/skills/create-slide-deck/` — creates and validates decks in the shared library.
- `.claude/skills/edit-slide-deck/` — revises decks while preserving metadata and live preview behavior.
- `.claude/skills/create-slide/`, `slide-authoring/`, `create-theme/`, `apply-comments/`, and `current-slide/` — OpenSlide's supplied authoring skills.

## Dependency model

The template intentionally contains no `node_modules` and no manual install script. Gamut runs `bun install` in the dashboard artifact directory, then runs:

```text
open-slide dev --host 0.0.0.0 --no-skills-check
```

This avoids npm's `chmod` failure on Windows-backed 9p/drvfs workspaces and keeps dependency lifecycle under Gamut's dashboard manager.

## Validation

```bash
bun install --cwd /workspace/artifacts/open-slide-studio --frozen-lockfile
bun run --cwd /workspace/artifacts/open-slide-studio build
```

The dashboard uses Gamut's mounted-path mode, so OpenSlide's HTTP routes and HMR WebSocket remain under the agent artifact path without custom routing shims.

agents.name: Outbound Campaign Agent
agents.description: Runs an end-to-end personalized outbound motion: ICP qualification, sourcing, enrichment, fail-closed suppression, linted drafting, capped sending, cadence, reply detection, and calendar-sourced meeting reporting. Vendor-neutral through swappable adapters.
agents.details:
# Outbound Agent Template

A complete, vendor-neutral outbound motion you import as an agent and configure for your own team: ICP, positioning, tools, senders, caps, cadence, and voice.

It is not a copywriting prompt. Most of what is here is the machinery that decides who gets contacted, who never does, how often, from which mailbox, and what has to be true before a message is allowed out. That machinery is the part that is expensive to rebuild and easy to get quietly wrong.

## Start here

```bash
uv run --with pyyaml .claude/skills/agent-onboarding/scripts/list_adapters.py
```

Then ask the agent to run onboarding. It interviews you and writes `config/outbound.yaml`.

Nothing else runs until that file exists. That is deliberate.

## Example prompts

- Run onboarding and write my outbound config
- Qualify this account list against my ICP
- Draft today's capped batch and show me the lint results

## What you get

| | |
|---|---|
| **Onboarding skill** | A structured interview that writes your config, generates your `AGENTS.md`, seeds positioning files, initializes the database, and self-tests the wiring. |
| **Campaign skill** | Intake, drafting briefs, the send gate, the cadence tick, a capped manual LinkedIn queue, calendar-sourced meeting tracking, reporting. |
| **Adapter layer** | Seven capability slots. Swap a vendor without touching the motion. |
| **Enforcement** | A copy linter, a send-cap governor, a fail-closed suppression chain, and a do-not-touch gate, all of which run before a message can leave. |
| **Reporting** | Metrics and a zero-dependency dashboard, with meetings read from the sender's calendar rather than inferred from replies. No open tracking, by design. |

## The design decision worth knowing about

**Configuration is the single source of truth, and `AGENTS.md` is generated from it.**

The usual failure of an agent template is drift: the instructions say one thing, the code does another, and nobody notices for a month. Here the standing instructions are rendered from `config/outbound.yaml`, so a cap change or an ICP change updates both at once. If the two ever disagree, the config wins and you regenerate.

The second decision follows from the first: **rules that matter are enforced mechanically, not asked for politely.** An instruction not to use em dashes is a suggestion a model will occasionally ignore. A linter that refuses the send is not. The same applies to daily caps, suppression, and the approval gate on a campaign's first batch.

## Layout

```
config/
  outbound.example.yaml   every field, documented inline. Your config is merged over it.
  outbound.yaml           yours. Written by onboarding. The source of truth.
lib/
  config.py     typed access, brand embargo, send windows, per-sender caps with ramp
  adapters.py   the registry and the slot contract
  db.py         vendor-neutral SQLite schema
  identity.py   name and LinkedIn matching. Stops same-first-name coworker swaps.
  icp.py        tiering, size bands, disqualifiers, buyer tiers
  linter.py     mechanical copy enforcement
  caps.py       daily gate, stacked-rate governor, deliverability kill switch
  gates.py      the do-not-touch gate
adapters/
  sourcing/ enrichment/ sender/ crm/ calendar/ suppression/ notify/
.claude/skills/
  agent-onboarding/    the interview and its scripts
  outbound-campaign/      the runtime
positioning/
  positioning.md, use-cases.json, voice-samples.md    yours to fill in
```

## Adapters

Seven slots. Each is a directory of interchangeable modules, and **the vendor in each slot is the importing team's choice, not the template's.** Onboarding asks slot by slot which tools the team uses, as multiple choice from `adapters/catalog.yaml` (the most common real-world answers) plus an open "Other".

| Slot | Does | Reference implementation |
|---|---|---|
| `sourcing` | produce prospect rows | `csv` |
| `enrichment` | resolve contact data | `apollo` |
| `sender` | deliver, and report replies | `gmail` (`dryrun` is the starting mode) |
| `crm` | look up and record | `sqlite` (local) |
| `calendar` | report booked meetings | `google` |
| `suppression` | decide who is off limits | `crm`, `local` |
| `notify` | reach a human | `slack` |

The shipped modules are working reference implementations, not the menu. A vendor with no builtin (Outlook, Instantly, Attio, Calendly, anything) gets a stub via `scaffold_adapter.py`: the config names the team's real stack immediately, and the stub fails closed on every call until implemented. `none` disables a slot as a visible gap.

`enrichment` and `suppression` take an ordered list and run as a waterfall.

Writing a new adapter means implementing two or three functions and declaring which environment variables it needs. `lib/adapters.py` documents the contract at the top. The motion does not change when a vendor does.

## The rules that cannot be configured away

These are enforced in code, and `validate_config.py` fails a config that tries to disable them.

- **A reply stops the cadence.** Every reply, including ambiguous ones. A human decides whether to re-engage.
- **Suppression is fail-closed.** If a suppression source is unreachable, the run halts. Contacting a current customer as a cold prospect is worse than a delayed batch.
- **The first batch of a campaign needs human approval.**
- **The first run is a dry run, reviewed by a human.**
- **No tracking pixels, no link wrappers, no open tracking.** They damage deliverability for exactly the low-volume senders this template is built for, and the number they produce has been unreliable since Apple Mail Privacy Protection.
- **No rate is displayed without its denominator.** Below the configured floor, you get the raw count.

## Testing it

The sender defaults to `dryrun`, so the entire motion is exercisable with zero network calls and zero risk.

```bash
uv run --with pyyaml .claude/skills/agent-onboarding/scripts/selftest.py
```

Walks fixture prospects through config load, adapter resolution, identity matching, ICP qualification, cap enforcement, the linter, and the database write path. A missing vendor credential is reported as *not provisioned*, not as a failure, because the wiring is sound either way.

A pass means the machinery is correct. It says nothing about whether your ICP or your copy is any good. Only you can judge those.

## What this does not do

- It does not write your copy unattended. The drafting brief assembles the material; the agent writes the message; the linter gates it; you approve the first batch.
- It does not warm mailboxes. New senders ramp from 10 to 25 a day over roughly four weeks, but you need a real warmup provider and, past about 25 a day per mailbox, a dedicated sending domain.
- It does not give you an ICP. An inherited ICP reads plausible and targets the wrong people confidently. Empty and honest beats populated and wrong.

agents.details:
# Pipeline Doctor

> Stop forecasting on stale deals and start reviving the ones you gave up on too early.

## What it does

Pipeline Doctor is the CRM-honesty and revival specialist. It runs four routines against your own CRM and mailbox:

- **Weekly hygiene digest.** Flags open deals with past-due or repeatedly pushed close dates, deals that have gone quiet, missing amounts or contacts, and deals stuck in a stage longer than your own norm. Each flag comes with the specific fix, sorted so the biggest and latest-stage deals come first.
- **Stalled deal nudges.** Works out where each stalled deal stopped and who owes the next move, skips deals where you are genuinely waiting, and drafts a nudge with a concrete reason to reply. No "circling back".
- **Closed-lost win-back.** Every other week it finds deals lost for reasons that can change (timing, budget, no champion, a competitor) and checks for a real trigger such as new funding, a new leader, or a competitor stumble. When it finds one, it drafts a "why now" email and cites the source.
- **End-of-day CRM update.** Turns today's meetings, emails and calls with prospects into activity notes, next steps and suggested stage changes. It matches each one to the right deal, skips anything already logged, flags what is unclear, and waits for your approval.

Everything it writes to buyers is a draft in your own Gmail or Outlook. It never sends anything, and it never changes the CRM until you approve.

## What you'll need

- **A CRM:** HubSpot, Salesforce or Attio as a connected account, or Pipedrive or Close through their MCP servers. Required.
- **Gmail or Outlook:** required. Nudge and win-back drafts land in your own mailbox.
- **Google Calendar:** required for the end-of-day update (Outlook calendar also works).
- **Meeting notes:** optional. Granola, Fireflies, Otter, Gong, Fathom or Zoom make the end-of-day notes richer.
- **Delivery channel:** in-app, or the agent's own Slack app, email inbox, Telegram or iMessage for digests and approval batches.
- **API keys:** none. Web search and lead enrichment for win-back triggers are built in.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut. The `agent-onboarding` skill starts automatically.
2. Onboarding connects your CRM, mailbox and calendar. It reads your stages and computes how long deals normally sit in each one. Then it asks about your thresholds, opt-outs, where reports should go and how much to do without asking, and runs a dry pass on your real pipeline.
3. Ask for your first hygiene digest, then let the weekly schedules take over.

Re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

- Check my HubSpot pipeline and show me what is rotting
- Draft nudges for my stalled late-stage deals with a real reason to reply
- Every other Monday, find closed-lost deals worth reviving and draft emails

agents.description: Owns the proposal from discovery notes to signed contract: drafts it from the rate card, then runs a fixed follow-up cadence so no proposal goes cold.
agents.details:
# Proposal Pilot

> Go from call notes to a sendable proposal, priced from the rate card, and never let it go cold after it is sent.

## What it does

Proposal Pilot owns the proposal for founder-led consulting, accounting, insurance, and staffing firms. It starts from Granola, the CRM notes, or a pasted call summary and writes the proposal in your template: situation, scope, approach, timeline, price, and next step. Every price comes from the rate card, never a guess. It sends you the draft with gaps called out, then leaves the approved proposal in a Gmail draft for one-tap send.

After that, it tracks each deal through its milestones: discovery done, proposal sent, client reply, contract out, signed. It runs a fixed cadence instead of vague check-ins, by default follow-ups on days 2, 5, and 10 after the proposal and days 3 and 7 after the contract. Every follow-up is a draft in the original thread for your approval. It measures how fast proposals go out after discovery, flags anything slipping past its window, and proposes stage moves. It never marks a deal lost on its own.

Proposal Pilot writes the proposal. Its sibling, Quote Chaser, chases estimates that a home services shop has already sent.

## What you'll need

- **Granola** — recommended for call notes, through the Granola MCP. Other notes tools or pasted notes work too.
- **Google Drive** — required for the proposal template, the rate card, and the finished Doc.
- **HubSpot** — the supported CRM connector for deal stages and follow-up tasks. Another CRM or a Google Sheet can be configured during onboarding.
- **Gmail** — required for proposal and follow-up drafts, and to detect sends and replies.
- **Slack** — for the daily digest and gap lists, sent from the agent's own Slack app. Email or in-app also work.
- **API keys:** none.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut.
2. The `agent-onboarding` skill runs before first use. It asks for your proposal template, rate card, call notes source, stage mapping, follow-up cadence, speed target, and who approves price, then saves the answers into `AGENTS.md` and `.claude/skills/agent-onboarding/config.json`.
3. Ask for the first run: Turn the latest call notes into a sendable proposal, in draft. After you approve the dry run, it sets up the mail trigger and the daily cadence check.

Re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

- Turn my latest call notes into a sendable proposal from our template
- Which proposals are due a follow-up today, and which ones are slipping?
- After each discovery call in Granola, draft the proposal and Slack me the gaps

## What's inside

- `AGENTS.md` — the drafting, follow-up cadence, and weekly speed routines, the deal stages, the Gamut setup, safe operating rules, and the `## Your context` block that onboarding fills in.
- `.claude/skills/agent-onboarding/` — the first-run interview that captures your systems, stages, cadence, voice, and approval rules, runs a supervised draft, and schedules the runs.

## Notes

- Built for 2-200 person founder-led professional firms that still rebuild every proposal from a blank page.
- Proposals and follow-ups stay in draft until the founder one-tap sends. The agent never nudges more often than the configured cadence.

agents.description: Onboarding agent that reads your company website, suggests four starter tasks tailored to your role, and does the one you pick in your first session -- then offers to make it an always-on agent if it's worth repeating.
agents.details:
# Quick Start

> Give it your company's website and walk away from your first session with a real piece of work done, not a tour.

## What it does

Quick Start is a first-session guide for people who are new to Gamut and want to see it do something useful right away. It opens with one question: what is your company's website? It reads the homepage, works out what the company does and who it serves, and asks which role best describes your work there.

From that, it invents four starter tasks that could only exist for your company and your job, each sized to finish in a single session. Some run entirely in the browser with nothing connected; others use a work tool you choose at hand-off. Pick one and Quick Start does it while you watch, showing drafts and asking before anything is sent, posted, or changed.

If you already know what you want, skip the website question and just say it. Quick Start drops the onboarding and gets to work. When a task turns out to be something you would want every day or week, it offers once to set it up as an always-on agent and hands you the prompt.

## What you'll need

- **Accounts:** None are required. Browser-based tasks need nothing connected. If the task you pick uses email, calendar, chat, CRM, docs, or a project tracker, Quick Start asks which product you use and requests that one account.
- **API keys:** None.
- **Time:** A minute to give the website and pick a task, then a few minutes of watching it work.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut.
2. The first session starts automatically and runs the `agent-onboarding` skill, which asks for your company's website.
3. Answer the role question, pick one of the four starter tasks, and approve any account connection the task needs.

Later sessions behave like a normal assistant. Ask for the next starter task whenever you want another one.

## Example prompts

- Hey Gamut, I'm new here. What can you do for me?
- Read our website and suggest four tasks you could do for me today
- That worked, set it up to run for me every Monday morning

## What's inside

- `AGENTS.md` — the agent's durable role, voice, the fixed welcome opener, and style rules.
- `.claude/skills/agent-onboarding/` — the website read, role and task pickers, hand-off, and the format used when a task becomes an always-on agent.

## Privacy

Quick Start reads only your company's public homepage. It connects a work account only when the task you chose needs one, one account at a time, after asking. It never sends, posts, submits, or edits anything in a connected app without showing you first.

## Notes

- On a phone, Quick Start offers only tasks that run through connected apps, since browser work is easier to follow on a laptop.
- If the website is unreachable or too generic to learn from, it makes one gentle retry and then continues with default roles rather than blocking.

agents.details:
# Quote Chaser

> Sitting estimates get a follow-up in the shop voice until they are won, lost, or handed to you.

## What it does

Quote Chaser owns sitting estimates for founder-led home services shops. Every weekday morning it pulls open estimates from Jobber, Housecall Pro, ServiceTitan, or the quote sheet, and works out where each one stands: estimate sent, customer replied, paperwork out, won. Then it runs a fixed, configurable cadence instead of vague check-ins. By default that means nudges on days 2, 5, and 10 after the estimate goes out and days 3 and 7 after approval paperwork, then a founder call.

Each nudge is a short draft in the founder's voice that names the job, the date, and a clear next step: approve, pick a start window, or say no. It is queued in Gmail, the field-service tool, or the approval message for one-tap send. A reply pauses the cadence. The agent flags site visits with no estimate yet, estimates expiring this week, and anything slipping past its window. It never changes a quote amount, promises a discount, or marks a quote won or lost on its own.

Quote Chaser chases estimates your shop already sent. It does not write them. Its sibling, Proposal Pilot, writes and follows up professional-services proposals.

## What you'll need

- **Gmail** — required for follow-up drafts and to see replies. Outlook works too.
- **Slack** — for the daily digest of drafts to approve, sent from the agent's own Slack app. Email or in-app also work.
- **Jobber, Housecall Pro, or ServiceTitan** — one is needed for open estimates. No registry connector; connected during onboarding by API key or browser sign-in, or use a quote sheet.

## Getting started

2. The `agent-onboarding` skill runs before first use. It asks for your estimate system, the follow-up cadence, how soon estimates should go out after a visit, quiet hours for texts, and where the digest goes, then saves the answers into `AGENTS.md` and `.claude/skills/agent-onboarding/config.json`.
3. Ask for the first run: Review sitting estimates, draft follow-ups for the ones going cold, and queue one-tap sends without sending. After you approve, it schedules the daily chase.

## Example prompts

## What's inside

agents.details:
# Recruiter Desk

> Spend your day on candidate calls while the sourcing sheets, reply reads, scorecards and follow-up drafts get done in the background.

## What it does

Recruiter Desk is for agency and contract recruiters, and for in-house recruiters juggling several open roles. It runs six routines, each switched on or off on its own:

- **Candidate Sourcing Run**: on request, reads the job description, shows you a sourcing plan (titles, 10–20 target companies, location), then finds and enriches 20–50 real people with Clay or Gamut's built-in lead enrichment. Each person gets a 1–100 fit score, an archetype, a possible warm-referral teammate and a short outreach note in your voice, all in a ranked Google Sheet.
- **Candidate Reply Assessment**: when a candidate answers your outreach, scores how likely they are to take a screen on a fixed 0–100 scale, researches them through web search, and leaves you an internal read as a draft in the same thread. "Do not contact" requests are flagged at the top.
- **Post-Interview Candidate Follow-Up**: after an interview, drafts a specific, candidate-facing note for next round, still in process, or a kind pass.
- **Post-Interview Pipeline Update**: fills your scorecard in your ATS's exact format, writes clean notes, and suggests the stage change. Candid notes stay internal.
- **Hiring Manager Weekly Update**: one skimmable update per search, addressed to the right hiring manager or client, leading with movement, asks and at-risk flags.
- **Stalled Candidate Re-Engagement**: twice a week, finds good candidates who went quiet and drafts a nudge that picks up where you left off, using what they told you they care about.

It never contacts candidates or clients on its own. Everything addressed to someone else lands as a draft in your mailbox for you to review and send. It is the lightweight, routine-based option: for a full in-house pipeline with a calibrated screening filter, see Recruiting Agent; for scoring inbound applications, see Applicant Screener or Recruiting Reviewer.

## What you'll need

- **Gmail or Outlook**: required. Drafts land in your mailbox and the reply routine watches your outreach threads.
- **Google Calendar**: required for the post-interview routines and weekly updates.
- **Google Sheets**: required for sourcing sheets; also works as a simple tracker.
- **Greenhouse**: optional, as your ATS. Ashby or Lever also work with an API key, or through the browser if you have no key.
- **Clay**: optional, for sourcing and enrichment. Without it, Gamut's built-in lead enrichment is used.
- **Meeting notes**: optional. Granola, Fathom, Fireflies, Otter or Zoom transcripts make post-interview drafts specific.
- **API keys:** none for Greenhouse or Gmail. An Ashby or Lever API key if that is your ATS.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut.
2. Onboarding starts automatically with the `agent-onboarding` skill: pick your routines, connect your mailbox, calendar and ATS, share your scorecard, stage names and active searches, paste a few emails so drafts sound like you, and choose where alerts go.
3. It does a supervised dry run on your real data, then schedules the routines you switched on. Start with a sourcing run for one live role.

Re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

- Source 30 candidates for our senior backend engineer role and show me the plan
- Assess the latest candidate reply on my outreach and leave me a draft
- Every Friday at 8am, draft an update for each hiring manager on my searches

## What's inside

- `AGENTS.md`: the six routines, the Gamut mechanics, privacy rules and safe operating rules.
- `.claude/skills/agent-onboarding/`: first-run setup, connections, dry run and scheduling.
- `.claude/skills/reply-assessment-rubric/`: the fixed 0–100 likelihood scale and the internal assessment format.
- `.claude/skills/sourcing-sheet/`: the sourcing sheet columns, score bands and write procedure.

## Privacy

- Candidate data stays in the systems it came from (your mailbox, ATS and sourcing sheet). The agent's own run records keep only IDs, dates and scores.
- Research uses public professional information found through web search. It does not open LinkedIn profile pages directly or use people-search sites.
- It never records protected characteristics, and do-not-contact requests are honored in every routine and every future search.
- Internal notes, scores and comp details never go anywhere a candidate can see them. One client's candidates and pipeline are never shown to another client.

## Notes

- Nothing goes to a candidate or client automatically. Rejections and any held ATS stage moves always wait for your approval, because some ATS stage changes email candidates on their own.
- Enrichment uses credits. You approve the sourcing plan before any enrichment runs.
- If you recruit in the EU, UK or California, you may need to tell sourced candidates how their data was obtained. The agent reminds you and keeps sourcing sheets easy to purge.

# Release To Social Campaign

> Every customer-facing change your team ships gets a post, a changelog note, and an approver's yes before anything goes live.

## What it does

Release To Social Campaign watches GitHub releases, merged pull requests, Linear completed issues, or your changelog, and keeps only what a customer would notice. Internal refactors, dependency bumps, tests, and reverts are left out, with a short "left out" list so nothing disappears silently. Related changes are grouped into stories that lead with the customer benefit, not the implementation.

For each story it writes two formats you choose (a social post and a changelog note, or a blog blurb) and a separate version per platform rather than one post pasted everywhere. Drafts land in Postiz if you use it, otherwise in a Notion page or Google Doc. The approver gets one Slack message from the agent with the drafts, a proposed schedule, and a link back to each PR or issue so every claim can be checked.

- **Ship-to-campaign drafts** — on each release or merge, or a weekly sweep; never drafts the same item twice and stays quiet when nothing customer-facing shipped.
- **Approval and scheduling** — per-draft approval from the named approver; only approved drafts are scheduled in Postiz or handed over as copy-ready text.
- **72-hour performance summary** — per-post numbers from Postiz or your own X account, with "not available" where a platform can't be read.

Nothing is ever published, scheduled to go live, or posted without explicit approval of the exact draft.

## What you'll need

- **GitHub** — required (or Linear or a changelog page as the shipping source). Reads releases and merged pull requests.
- **Linear** — optional, for completed issues and projects.
- **Slack** — recommended. The agent's own Slack app sends review messages to the approver. Its own email inbox, Telegram, or in-app also work.
- **Notion or Google Docs** — where drafts land when Postiz isn't used.
- **Postiz** — optional, through a Postiz API key; drafts are created there and scheduled only after approval.
- **X or LinkedIn** — optional, your own account, read-only, for the performance summary.
- **API keys:** `POSTIZ_API_KEY` only if you use Postiz.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut and send the setup message waiting in your message box.
2. The `agent-onboarding` skill connects your sources and draft destination, asks which releases count, which accounts post, who approves, and your voice, then runs a drafts-only test on one past release.
3. Once you're happy with the test, it sets up the release trigger or a weekly sweep.

Re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

- Draft a campaign from our last GitHub release as a test

## What's inside

agents.details:
# Renewal Clerk

> Every contract end date is tracked and every renewal is drafted before the term quietly dies.

## What it does

Renewal Clerk owns contract renewals for founder-led consulting, accounting, insurance, staffing and law firms, on both sides: the contracts clients pay you for and the contracts you pay vendors for. It keeps a living tracker with counterparty, annual value, renewal date, an auto-renew yes/no flag, and the notice-period deadline, which is the real date you have to act by and often falls 30 to 90 days before the renewal date.

When a new contract, order form or renewal notice lands in your inbox, it reads the attachment itself, not just the email, and adds or updates the tracker. A contract whose terms it could not read is flagged as a data hole, never guessed.

It alerts you ahead of every notice deadline with enough lead time to decide, with big-ticket and auto-renewing contracts first. For clients it pulls the usage picture where one is connected and drafts the renewal note and next-term order form from your template and current price. For vendors it shows a decision card and drafts the non-renewal or renegotiation email you ask for. Nothing auto-renews, nothing is cancelled, and no email goes out without your approval.

## What you'll need

- **Google Drive** — required for the contract folder and the order form template. Dropbox, Box or OneDrive work too.
- **Gmail or Outlook** — required. New contracts and renewal notices are read from your inbox and drafts land there.
- **Google Sheets** — recommended, if you want the tracker as a sheet you can see.
- **HubSpot** — optional, for customer contract records and renewal logging. Salesforce or Attio work too.
- **Slack** — the agent posts alerts from its own Slack app, set up during onboarding. Your own Slack account is only needed if it should read a channel.
- **Google Calendar** — optional, for a hold on each act-by date.
- **Usage or billing system** — optional, for the client usage picture. Connected during onboarding; no registry connector.
- **API keys:** none required.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut.
2. The `agent-onboarding` skill runs before first use. It connects your contract folder and mailbox, asks which sides to track, your alert lead times, big-ticket threshold, usage source and renewal voice, parses a first batch of contracts with you, and schedules the sweeps, alerts and the new-contract watch.
3. Ask for the first run: build the tracker, list notice deadlines in the next 120 days, and draft customer renewals that are due, without sending.

Re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

## What's inside

# Reply Drafter

## What it does

Every weekday morning, Reply Drafter checks your mentions and the replies to your posts since its last run, a watch list of people you're building relationships with, and a few topics you care about. It keeps only the 3 to 5 posts that genuinely deserve your time: a mention that needs a response, a question you can answer well, a conversation you should join, or a relationship worth investing in.

For each one you get a one-line reason, a link to the post, and a starting reply or quote post written in your voice, learned from replies you're proud of. It skips engagement bait, giveaways, rage-bait, crowded threads, and anything you already answered, never shows you the same post twice, and sends nothing when nothing clears the bar.

It never posts, replies, likes, reposts, follows, or sends a DM on X. Every reply is yours to rewrite and send.

agents.name: SaaS Spend Auditor
agents.description: Audits company software subscriptions monthly against real usage, ranks savings, and tracks renewal notice dates. Never cancels or downgrades.
agents.details:
# SaaS Spend Auditor

> Find the software your team pays for and doesn't use, and catch every renewal while you can still say no.

## What it does

Once a month, SaaS Spend Auditor pulls recurring charges from Ramp or Brex, or from your accounting system or a card export, and looks back 13 months so annual plans don't hide. It rolls spend up by vendor with amount, cadence and change against prior months, and cleans up messy card descriptors along the way.

Then it looks for usage evidence: paid seats against active users where admin data is reachable, activity from admin exports you share, and softer signals such as mentions in email, Slack and the calendar. It flags tools with no use in 30 days, excess seats, renewals and price increases, duplicate tools, trials that turned into paid plans, and the same vendor paid on several cards. The digest is ranked by potential savings and split into "probably cancel" and "worth a closer look". Each item says how strong the evidence is and when the saving can actually be realized.

It also tracks renewal notice deadlines, which usually fall 30-90 days before the renewal itself, and warns you while there's still time to act. It never cancels, downgrades, changes seats or contacts a vendor.

## What you'll need

- **Ramp** or **Brex**: one spend source, through their MCP servers. QuickBooks, Xero or a card export work instead.
- **Gmail**: recommended, for renewal and signup emails and usage signals.
- **Slack**: optional, for tool mentions and, if you're an admin, inactive members.
- **Google Sheets**: optional, for a shared subscription inventory.
- **Google Calendar**: optional, for meeting-tool usage and notice-deadline reminders.
- **Admin access or exports** for tools like GitHub, Zoom, HubSpot or Notion: optional, for the strongest seat-usage evidence.
- **API keys:** none.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut.
2. The `agent-onboarding` skill runs on first use. It asks where software gets paid for, where usage can be seen, your thresholds and keep-list, how early to warn about notice deadlines, and where the digest goes. Then it connects your accounts and runs a supervised first review.
3. Ask for your first review: "Find software we're paying for but not using."

Re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

- Find software we're paying for in Ramp but nobody has used in 30 days
- Which SaaS renewals have notice deadlines in the next 60 days?
- On the 1st of every month, email me the ranked subscription savings digest

## What's inside

- `AGENTS.md`: the monthly waste review and the renewal notice watch, with their domain details, connection and scheduling mechanics, and safe operating rules.
- `.claude/skills/agent-onboarding/`: first-run setup that writes `config.json` and creates both schedules.
- `.claude/skills/spend-rollup/`: vendor normalization, cadence detection, usage-evidence grades, savings math and notice-deadline rules.

## Notes

- Report only. Cancelling, downgrading and vendor contact are always your call. Check-ins to tool owners are drafted and held for approval.
- "No usage signal found" is not the same as "unused", and the digest always says which one it means.
- For personal subscriptions found in Gmail receipts, see the sibling Subscription Pruner template.

## Privacy

The agent reads card transactions, email, Slack and calendar metadata only to judge whether a tool is used. The subscription inventory stays in the agent's workspace, or in your sheet if you choose one.

agents.details:
# SEO Agent — template

An autonomous SEO specialist that owns one website's organic growth end to end:

- **Content engine** — a prioritized backlog burned down daily: keyword-researched,
  multi-angle-researched, fact-checked, humanized articles published through your CMS,
  plus on-site "surface" improvements (metas, internal links, structured data).
- **Link building** — competitor-backlink prospecting, directory/listing submissions,
  and (optionally) personalized email outreach with a local CRM, ramp caps, and
  follow-up discipline.
- **Technical SEO** — a monthly comprehensive audit (sitemap, indexing, redirects,
  performance, structured data) that ends in PRs or tickets, not just findings.
- **Strategy & reporting** — a weekly steering session that pulls KPIs, replenishes
  backlogs, and sends a one-page report by email or Slack; a live **SEO Master
  dashboard** (Ahrefs + Search Console + program activity).

## What it needs

| Requirement | Used for | Required? |
|---|---|---|
| **Ahrefs API key** (plan with API access; Site Explorer endpoints ideally) | Keyword research, backlink/DR tracking, competitor analysis | Yes (SEMrush possible with skill edits) |
| **Google Search Console** service account added to the property | Clicks/impressions/rankings — the north-star metrics | Yes |
| **CMS or repo access** (Sanity/WordPress/Ghost/git/hosted builder) | Publishing content | Yes, for the content engine |
| **Gmail (connected account)** | Weekly report by email; outreach inbox (ideally a dedicated inbox on a separate warmed domain) | Optional |
| **Slack (chat integration)** | Weekly report via Slack instead of email | Optional |
| **GitHub (connected account)** | Site PRs, awesome-list submissions | Optional |
| **Unsplash API key** | Blog imagery (Openverse works keyless) | Optional |

## What onboarding does

Importing this template auto-launches a setup session (the `agent-onboarding` skill):

1. **Tools** — connects GSC + Ahrefs (offers to drive signup in the browser if you have
   neither), confirms the domain, kicks off an Ahrefs site audit.
2. **Research** — explores your website, current rankings and backlinks, and your
   competitors; presents a baseline analysis; agrees a keyword list with you (with a
   light primer on head vs tail terms and search intent).
3. **Plan** — technical audit scheduling, link-building approach, content cadence and
   backlog, plus 1–2 creative ideas for your specific business; agrees goals/targets.
4. **Cadences** — schedules the daily content / daily links / weekly strategy / monthly
   audit tasks, connects the report channel (email/Slack), and verifies the dashboard
   renders with your data.

Nothing is published, sent, or merged without an explicit autonomy grant you make
during onboarding (recorded in `seo/STATE.md`).

## Example prompts

- Show me the SEO dashboard and this week's numbers
- Publish the next article from the content backlog
- Run the monthly technical audit and open the PRs

## Layout

```
AGENTS.md                  agent instructions (generic; onboarding personalizes)
.env.example               required/optional secrets
seo/                       program state: config.json, STATE.md, backlogs, CRM, log
artifacts/seo-master/      the SEO dashboard (React + Bun; collector-fed)
.claude/skills/            11 skills (see AGENTS.md for the table)
```

Upload the zip as a new agent template / import it as an agent workspace. The onboarding
session starts automatically. Have your Ahrefs key handy; GSC setup can be done together
during onboarding.

agents.name: Side Project Monitor
agents.description: Owns daily monitoring for a side project: picks the metrics worth watching, catches cost spikes, drop-offs and regressions early, and suggests what to build next.
agents.details:
# Side Project Monitor

> Production-grade monitoring for the project you build on weekends, in one short morning brief that tells you what to do and what can wait.

## What it does

Side Project Monitor watches a side project you don't have time to check. Every morning it reads your product analytics, the GitHub repo and, if you connect them, Stripe and your hosting, database, error-tracking and AI API costs. It then sends a brief that opens with a one-line verdict, then lists what needs action now, what to look at this week, and what went well.

You don't have to tell it what to watch. It proposes the 6 to 10 signals that matter for your project, such as activation, retention, failed payments, cost per active user and error rate after each deploy, and you confirm the list. It keeps a rolling baseline, so it can tell a real cost spike, drop-off or regression from the normal ups and downs of small numbers. When a metric breaks right after a deploy, it links the commit.

Each brief ends with up to two improvement ideas drawn from the data: a feature new users try and then abandon, a busy page people leave, a request that keeps coming up in issues. It only reads and reports. It never changes code, settings or billing.

## What you'll need

- **PostHog or Google Analytics**: one is strongly recommended, for traffic, activation, funnels and retention.
- **GitHub**: required, read only, for commits, deploys, CI status, security alerts and issues.
- **Stripe**: optional, for MRR, failed payments, cancellations and disputes.
- **Hosting, database and error tracking**: optional. Vercel, Supabase, Sentry and similar services connect through whatever the app offers, or a read-only token you create.
- **Slack, email, Telegram or iMessage**: optional. The agent's own account delivers the brief; otherwise it stays in the app.
- **API keys:** only for infra services with no other connection option, for example `VERCEL_TOKEN`, `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` or `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, with read-only scopes.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut.
2. The `agent-onboarding` skill runs on first use. It connects the repo and analytics, detects your hosting from the repo, asks about payments, budget and plan limits, proposes a watchlist for you to confirm, and fills in 28 days of baseline history.
3. Review a first brief on yesterday's data, then let the daily schedule run.

Re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

- How did my project do yesterday, and does anything need me?
- What metrics should I be watching that I'm not, and why?
- Every morning at 8, send me the brief and alert me on any cost spike

## What's inside

- `AGENTS.md`: the watchlist, daily brief and optional cost-watch routines, connection table, schedules, state files and the `## Your context` block.
- `.claude/skills/agent-onboarding/`: first-run setup for sources, budget, watchlist, baseline, delivery and schedule.
- `.claude/skills/metrics-baseline/`: the metric menu, baseline format and flag rules for cost, revenue, funnels and regressions.

## Notes

- Read only. It never opens pull requests, deploys, changes hosting or billing settings, refunds or rotates keys.
- Small projects have small numbers, so traffic and funnel alerts need a minimum volume. Cost and payment alerts are the most sensitive and can go out between briefs if you enable the cost watch.
- An optional home-screen widget can show one key number, such as weekly active users or MRR, with its trend.

agents.name: Target Account Radar
agents.description: Watches target accounts, contacts, competitors and topics for real buying signals; sends a cited digest and high-bar X alerts, each with an outreach angle.
agents.details:
# Target Account Radar

> Always have a timely, specific reason to reach out to the accounts you care about most.

## What it does

Target Account Radar watches a list you can edit: target accounts, their key people, competitors and industry topics. It watches the web and X for real buying signals: funding, acquisitions, leadership changes, launches, earnings, hiring surges or layoffs, press, and notable posts. It also watches for sub-industry trends that create urgency for what you sell.

- **Account digest.** Weekly by default, or daily. Grouped by account, with account news first and industry signals after. Each item has a source link and date, why it matters, and a suggested outreach angle or opening line. Stale, repeated and unsourced items are dropped.
- **X watch.** A couple of times a day it checks the people and topics you track on X. It messages you only when something clears a high bar, such as a launch, a funding announcement, a new executive, or a pointed critique of a competitor. If nothing does, you hear nothing.

It researches and suggests. It never sends outreach and never posts on X.

## What you'll need

- **Google Sheets or Google Docs:** required for the editable watchlist, unless the list lives in your CRM.
- **HubSpot or Salesforce:** optional, to read target accounts from a CRM list. Attio, Pipedrive and Close also work.
- **X:** built-in public X reads work with no account. They are billed per post read, so queries stay narrow. Connect your own X account (`twitter`) if you prefer to use it.
- **Delivery channel:** in-app, or the agent's own Slack app, email inbox, Telegram or iMessage.
- **API keys:** none. Web search, Exa and lead enrichment are built in.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut. The `agent-onboarding` skill starts automatically.
2. Onboarding builds or connects your watchlist and learns what you sell. It sets the signal bar, the digest cadence, the X check times and a monthly X budget, then picks where alerts go and runs a first digest on your top accounts.
3. Review the first digest, tighten the list, and let the schedules run.

Re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

- Start a watchlist sheet from these ten accounts and their CEOs
- What happened at my target accounts this week, and how should I open?
- Watch these founders on X twice a day and ping me only on big news

## What's inside

- `AGENTS.md`: the digest and X watch routines, Gamut mechanics, and safe operating rules.
- `.claude/skills/agent-onboarding/`: first-run setup, dry run, schedules and config.
- `.claude/skills/signal-bar/`: the freshness gate, signal strength table, outreach-angle formula and X query hygiene.

## Notes

- X recent search only reaches back about seven days. The watch checks steadily and cannot catch up after a long pause.
- Built-in X reads cost money per post. Onboarding gives a rough monthly estimate and sets a ceiling.
- For a deep weekly rundown on a single account, pair with `account-media-rundown`. For LinkedIn leaders, pair with `linkedin-signal-watch`.

## Privacy

Target Account Radar reads only public web and X content, plus the watchlist you give it. It keeps a ledger of links and post ids it has already reported, so nothing is reported twice. It never contacts anyone.

agents.description: Builds and keeps your team's shared brain, a folder of pages people and agents read to understand the team, with you in a collaborative research loop, then maintains it daily and improves itself.
agents.details:
# Team Brain

Builds and keeps your team's **brain**: a shared folder of pages that people and AI agents read to understand the team. That means who it is, what it does, how it works, what it has decided, and where everything else lives.

## How it works

- **Build** (`build-brain`): a collaborative session. The agent researches the team, asks you for sources and the knowledge only you have, and writes the brain as it goes, so you can watch it take shape, redirect it, and leave and come back without losing anything. Run it again any time to add context or refine the brain.
- **Answer and absorb:** ask it anything about the team, or send it something to add. Other agents read the brain and message it to add or correct something, because only it writes the brain.
- **Glossary:** one table of the team's terms, with what to say to each audience, so people and agents use the same words. If you already keep one, the brain links it instead.
- **Now and how-to:** optional pages for what the team is focused on now, refreshed every upkeep, and, when the team works through shared agents, one page per task saying which agent to ask.
- **Read-only:** connected to a folder managed elsewhere, such as another workspace's Team Brain or a shared folder of docs, it only answers questions from it.
- **Maintain** (`maintain-brain`): a scheduled upkeep task. It retries pending contributions, checks the brain's health and staleness, re-syncs sources, learns from your edits, reflects on recent sessions to improve its own skills, and reports only when something changed or you're needed. When a Needs-you item is for one specific person, it tags them, so they're notified. It also tells you when a newer version of this template is out.
- **Update** (`update-from-template`): say "update from template" and it compares itself with the latest published template, shows you what it would take and what it would keep, and applies the plan once you agree.

## Getting started

1. Attach an empty shared folder for the brain to this agent.
2. Start a conversation. The build begins right away.

Importing the template doesn't connect any accounts or start any schedules. Setting up Team Brain creates the one upkeep task, on the schedule you pick.

agents.name: Team Progress Digest
agents.description: Daily read-only digest of what your human team shipped, has in progress, and is stuck on, from GitHub and Linear or Jira, with every item linked.
agents.details:
# Team Progress Digest

> See what your team shipped and where they are stuck every morning, without asking anyone for a status update.

## What it does

Team Progress Digest reads your team's pull requests in GitHub and issues in Linear or Jira, and every weekday morning sends you one short digest:

- **Needs you** — questions addressed to you, items labeled as waiting on a decision, reviews requested from you, and anything blocked on you.
- **Stuck** — PRs waiting on review, failing checks, conflicts, and issues that have sat in progress or review past your thresholds, each with how long it has been stuck.
- **Shipped** — merged to the default branch or completed, with the PR and its issue shown together.
- **In progress** — what is actively moving.

Items are grouped by project or by person, and every line links to the PR or issue. Dependency-update PRs collapse to one line. An optional Friday digest adds the week's synthesis, a few computed measures such as review wait time, and up to three evidence-backed signals worth watching.

It is strictly read-only and is not a performance tool: it never ranks people by output. For a summary of what AI agents did, use Swarm Daily Summarizer instead.

## What you'll need

- **GitHub** — required if your team uses GitHub. Read as you, or through the agent's own GitHub app scoped to the repos you choose.
- **Linear** — or **Jira**, for issues, projects, and blocked relations. GitHub Issues alone also works.
- **A delivery channel** — the agent's own Slack app (a DM to you or a team channel), its own email inbox, Telegram, or iMessage. In-app only also works.
- **API keys:** none.

## Getting started

1. Import the template into Gamut.
2. The `agent-onboarding` skill runs before first use. It connects GitHub and your tracker, picks the repos, teams, and people in scope, sets what counts as stuck and how decisions are labeled, and chooses when and where the digest arrives.
3. It builds a digest for the last two business days as a supervised dry run, then schedules the daily run and the optional Friday digest.

Re-run onboarding anytime by asking the agent to run the `agent-onboarding` skill.

## Example prompts

- What did the team ship yesterday, and what is stuck right now?
- Show me every PR waiting on review for more than two days
- Every Friday at 4pm, send me the weekly digest with what to watch

## What's inside

- `AGENTS.md` — the daily and weekly digests, Gamut mechanics, and safe operating rules.
- `.claude/skills/agent-onboarding/` — first-run setup that connects sources, sets scope and thresholds, schedules the digests, and writes `config.json`.
- `.claude/skills/stuck-signals/` — stuck and waiting-on-decision rules, plus the GitHub, Linear, and Jira queries and PR-to-issue linking.

## Notes

- Monday's digest covers Friday through Monday morning. If a source cannot be read, the digest says so instead of reporting a quiet day.
- Stuck items go to you privately by default. Posting to a team channel is opt-in.
